Review Text:
So we booked this through the Xanterra site that you get when you go to the Grand Canyon National Park site and look for activities. Right now it says that it's not available: what happened to us is that it was unavailable until spring, when they settle on the price etc. for the new tourist season. I asked to be put on an email notification so that it wouldn't sell out on the two days we had available in September, and that worked out. I was pretty persistent about checking on it with Xanterra.
First of all, it's a really, really long day. Just be prepared for that. You get up super early to drive over and check in, then wait at the airport for the sun to rise. The plane ride over the canyon was amazing: views that were so beautiful they made me cry. I appreciated that we both got window seats with an empty middle seat between us. There are headphones with recorded narration.
After flying over the canyon and Horseshoe Bend, you land at Lake Powell airport. We took pictures with the plane, had a bathroom break in the small airport, then met up with our Navajo nation guide for the trip to Antelope Canyon. She was very kind, patient, and welcoming. The ride is in an open air truck with two rows of bench seats. There is an overhead cover and there are seat belts. She took us into the area and then up to the canyon. I was a little worried because multiple buses pulled up and lots of people got out, but the guides handled it beautifully. Each group waited while the one ahead went into each area, took photos while listening to the guide, and then moved ahead. Very well organized. I had never been in a slot canyon and it was truly beautiful and very cool. The photos were amazing; our guide was full of tips about phone settings and positions in the canyon for various types of pictures.
We were taken to a water sports/activities center where we could refill water bottles and use the restroom while we waited outside. It was a little awkward. There we met up with another group and went through metal detectors before boarding a bus to the Lake Powell dam. At the foot of the dam we got into small open boats and floated down the Colorado river and around Horseshoe Bend, stopping to look at rock formations, wild horses (!), and views along the way. We got out of the boats once at a spot that had porta potties and amazingly clear Native American hieroglyphics. The water was too cold for swimming unless you were very hardy. The float trip was lovely, but a bit long since you couldn't move around very much on the boat and it was very sunny/hot. Also, the lunch provided was okay but not much....and they gave it to us while we were waiting for the bus and told us not to eat it on the bus, so we started eating before the bus and had to stop...it was strangely inefficient and not enough food for the day. Bring snacks and refill your water whenever you get the chance.
Bus ride home was worst part; comfortable but long with only one stop. Those of us who had done the plane part of the trip had to wait as the bus wound its way through Grand Canyon Village and slowly disembarked the others, so very late getting back to our vehicle and a really long time between bathroom breaks! (Also, the airport is pretty much closed when you get back so don't expect a bathroom there.)
All in all, a long day but so many great experiences!

Review Text:
This tour is worth every cent. We were picked up promptly from our hotel, then taken to the airfield. Checked in and boarded our small plane to fly out to the South Rim of the Grand Canyon. The weather was 45 degrees, so very hot, but they got flying quickly. Flew over the hoover dam and Lake Mead before arriving at the Canyon.

Then we were put into an open air hummer for a 2 hour tour. This was great, stopped at lots of lookouts, the guide took lots of photos. Given a delicious, fresh lunch to enjoy overlooking the south rim of the canyon.

After lunch we were taken to a heliport for a helicopter ride out to and over the canyon - breathtaking. Then flown back to Las Vegas in the light plane.

Only downside was upon checkin, they advised us that the price of fuel had increased so it would therefore be an extra $33pp - would have been nice to have been told beforehand, rather than right there on the spot - we couldn't back out, not that we would have, but given the price of this tour, I think some correspondence would have been nice.

Review Title: NOT TO BE MISSED, PANORAMA IS WORTH THE EXPENSE
Review Text:
Absolutely to book in advance because you can't do without it.
We booked it a few days before and called to confirm the reservation.
In June 2023 we spent 164 euros each for the flight + 14 euros each for fuel surcharge, it's a lot but the excursion is worth it all.
Having arrived at the airport half an hour early, there was a terrible wind blowing and we were asked if we still wanted to fly as there would have been strong turbulence and if we preferred to cancel they would refund the cost of the tickets.
We asked if we would fly safely, in which case we would have preferred to fly now we were there and we couldn't postpone it as it was an itinerant trip.
It shook so much that you risked crashing your camera into the window, every now and then several driving alarms began to sound and several warning lights came on.
The flight lasts about 40 minutes and was quite challenging and towards the end we had become quiet and a tried...
But I guarantee it was worth it, if I could go back I would do it again without a doubt and I highly recommend it.
From above you have the perception of the earth's crust and the crack that passes through it, it is a completely different image from the one you get when seeing the grand canyon from the various panoramic points on the edge.
I don't want to diminish the beauty of the grand canyon from the views, but in my opinion the flight completes the experience, absolutely worth the money spent.
The plane is honestly dated and the headphone supports and the regulators for the audio guide are now falling to pieces, a little more maintenance could be done on the internal instruments, but I realize that it will always be in flight and the time available is not much, but given the expense one would expect better maintained instruments.
Our flight had 8 seats and we all sat at the window.

Review Text:
We had originally thought about doing a helicopter trip of the Canyon, but several people who'd visited suggested the airplane tour was better. We decided to go for it and weren't disappointed.

We managed to book for 11am the following day which suited our schedule perfectly and arrived at their smart reception area at 10:20 as requested.

We were met by the pilot at 10:45 who showed us out to the waiting Cessna Grand Caravan. This is a perfect airplane for this type of trip since it is high-wing and affords an excellent view. Each of the comfortable seats was equipped with good-quality headsets so one could listen to the commentary throughout. The airplane was not too noisy, and it was still possible to hold a conversation with someone on the opposite side of the airplane (after removing the headset of course).

We were soon in the air and flying over the rim of the canyon. It takes a circular clockwise route and covers around 100 miles of the north and south sides of the canyon with excellent views including the Colorado river.

We returned for a very smooth landing around 40 minutes later.

Overall, this was an excellent experience at a reasonable price with plenty of opportunities to take great photos and videos. I would highly recommend it.

One minor gripe - we were asked to pay a $15 per person fuel surcharge at reception and I consider it would be better to incorporate this into the published price.

Review Text:

The raft ride on the Colorado through Glen canyon was really nice, though as others have mentioned, would have been nicer at an hour shorter duration. Our boat captain was quite knowledgeable and taught us a lot.
Oscar our bus driver was amazing! Friendly, personable with lots of great information and suggestions and an excellent driver!
A point of constructive criticism - when I first booked the trip, the booking agent told me to be sure to pack bathing suits for a dip in the Colorado River during the raft ride. When grand canyon airlines called to confirm a day before the trip, I tried to confirm the bathing suit need and asked about footwear for antelope canyon. I was told to absolutely NOT bring a bathing suit as the river was way too cold to swim in. I was very surprised when our raft captain offered the opportunity to take a dip in the river - which both my boys did in their clothes!
That all said - sneakers are plenty adequate for antelope canyon (I wore hiking boots) and definitely bring a bathing suit for a potential dip in the Colorado River (yes it was cold, but tolerable and refreshing in the shallows.) Sunscreen, water and a good sun hat are highly recommended!

Review Text:
As we had hoped, this was the highlight of our entire trip, but you need some advance knowledge and preparation. Read the cancellation policy closely when you book—no refunds for any reason.

This is a “Frankenstein” tour: 3 different tours by 3 different operators combined into a single package. You need mobility to do all these things: climb into/out of the plane, onto/off trucks, walk across loose sand and over rocks, and down narrow steps. The temperature can vary widely from dawn at the canyon rim to mid-day in Page to afternoon on the river. Dress in layers, and check the forecast highs & lows for the Grand Canyon/Tusayan and Page, AZ to plan how many layers!

The flight is early in the morning, probably to avoid winds and turbulence as things warm up. Check-in time was 6 a.m. Expect a phone call if you’re not there by 6:05. Their website says “2 meals included” but that is not the case--it’s BYOB (bring your own breakfast). You’ll meet your bus driver for later in the day, and seats on the plane will be assigned as necessary to balance the weight of the airplane.

The flight lasts about an hour. Headphones provide music and occasional narration in English, French, Spanish, and German. The pilot will S-turn along the canyon so both sides get good views thru the enlarged windows of the Grand Canyon, Glen Canyon, the Vermillion Cliffs, and Lake Mead. You’ll see Lee’s Ferry, Horseshoe Bend, and Glen Canyon Dam—all landmarks for your river trip.
After landing, we were met by our Antelope Canyon tour guide. We traveled to the canyon on bench seats in open-bed trucks—plan for wind, dust, and hot/cold. Masks are still required at all times on the Navajo reservation. If you’re lucky enough to get Tori as your canyon guide, she will not only point out the great photo spots, but also advise/help you to adjust the settings on your smartphone camera to get the best shots! The canyon tour lasts about an hour. Time permitting, you may get to clamber thru a smaller slot canyon which is much less accessible than the main canyon.

Next you return to Page, to the Wilderness River Adventures office. Don’t check in at their counter—your wristband shows you’re already processed and it will just confuse everybody. Your bus/van driver will show up and give you a run-down of the afternoon. You’ll be issued a box lunch, then process thru a TSA-like security check (You can leave non-compliant items and things you don’t want/need on the boating trip with your bus driver) prior to boarding a WRA bus to travel to the river.

The raft trip is smooth and relaxing. It lasts about 3 hours, with a stop after about 1.5 hours for lunch and to visit ancient pictograms. Our guide ‘Tia was cheerful and informative. At Lee’s Ferry, you’ll dock and meet your driver in the parking lot.

On the drive back to Tusayan (2-3 hrs), the bus will stop at Cameron Trading Post. You’ll only have 20 minutes or so to browse, so you might feel pressured to choose hastily. The selection seemed large (jewelry, pottery, blankets, leather, souvenirs), but prices seemed high. If you’re looking to buy jewelry your best strategy is to check the stores in Williams, AZ first (they focus on jewelry, with much smaller selections of pottery and other crafts). That way you can do a price/selection comparison.

Review Title: This is the way to tour the Grand Canyon
Review Text:
Trip Reserved: Grand Canyon Deluxe with Hummer
Our Group: 2 families (4 adults, 2 teenage boys)

On a recent trip to Las Vegas, we wanted the views of the South Rim without the 9 hour round trip drive from Vegas. After some searching I found this tour. It's not inexpensive, so we considered it for a while before booking.

I had been to the grand canyon twice. My husband and son never had. My husband's initial take was to simply do the 2.5 hour drive from Vegas to the West Rim, proclaiming "rocks are rocks."

In the end, knowing that the south rim is much more spectacular, we ended up booking this trip. It's a full day, that started with pick up at our hotel, and transfer to the Boulder City airport west of LV. From there we boarded an 8 passenger plane for a flight over the Hoover Dam, and part of the Grand Canyon before landing at the Grand Canyon Airport. The flight was narrated. Not by the pilot... there were headphones available and a pre-recorded narration in a few languages. It wasn't fantastic, but I appreciated that there was some narration to what we were seeing, and I did learn from it.

Once we landed, we transferred to open-air hummers for a several hour tour through several different vantage points in Grand Canyon National Park. Our tour guide was fantastic. His love of the GC is evident and comes through in his delivery. We had a boxed lunch (turkey sandwich, apple, chips, cookie, water). He had some fun suggestions for photos. He was very willing to play the role of photographer and take photos. And he was so knowledgeable and just had so much enjoyment about sharing "his Grand Canyon with us"

We returned via the same plane and were dropped off back at our hotel.

I don't know what could possibly make this anything other than a 5-star experience. If you have the means to take this tour, it is a wonderful way to experience one of the Natural Wonders of the World.

PS. Two teens on the trip. Pretty sure the only time they used their phones for the entire day was to take photos! You know that an experience that can accomplish that is a special one!

Review Text:
This was not a bad experience - but it was a little pricey for what you get.

The hotel pick up was fine. The driver was late. I called - repeatedly. Nobody answered. I was worried that we had somehow miscommunicated. Fortunately he was just running late. But it's a little disheartening to discover that there is nobody there if a problem develops.

They pick you up super early and drive you to the little airport. We sat there waiting for about 90 minutes before we boarded the plane. That's a lot of wasted time.

The flight was fine. They have twin engine Otters (those are the ones in the pictures) and single engine Cessnas. The Otters hold about 20 and the Cessnas hold about 10 so which plane you get on depends on how many passengers are flying. I suspect that some of the flight delays might be related to consolidating trips to fill the planes.

The flight itself was fine. It felt safe enough and fun if you haven't been on a small plane before. But you wear a headset and listen to an audio recording that sounds like it was made in the 1960s. Ours started late so it wasn't synced with what we were flying over. Then it glitched and started playing the safety briefing again. Then the pilot caught on and restarted the audio - from the start - so we were now way out of sync. Then he tried to zoom forward and it was a little better. But you get the idea - it's pretty canned.

The views of the grand canyon are good. You are much lower than any commercial flight so you see the ground much better but don't get a high level perspective. It's a big loop out and back trip. Most of the people on our flight were dozing off.

Bottom line, it wasn't bad, but it wasn't something I would do again.

Review Title: Enjoyed our Antelope Canyon & River Adventure
Review Text:
Our family of 5 did the Antelope Canyon & River Adventure tour, a 12 hour tour that leaves just after sunrise from the Tusayan airport, flies over the canyon in a fixed wing aircraft for about 45 minutes, then arrives in Page AZ. From there you do a guided tour of Antelope Canyon, and then take a smoothwater motorized river raft ride on the Colorado, followed by a bus ride back to the Canyon South Rim.
We had a partly cloudy day but the flight over the canyon was awesome! What a great way to see the Grand Canyon. There were unfortunately a number of nicks and scratches on most of the windows so that made it a little more challenging to get great photos but the flight was smooth (we got lucky there as the currents were calm) and the views were terrific.
We then were met at the Page airport by our Native American guide for the Antelope Canyon tour, and that was a real highlight. Our guide (unfortunately I forget her name) was terrific, not just sharing interesting information but also showing us how to get some spectacular photos that we would have never thought to take.
We then went on to the raft ride, which was just under four hours. Unfortunately we got there about an hour before the scheduled start time of the ride so we had to wait for a bit, but we were comfortable. The ride itself is about a 15 mile ride that takes a bit less than four hours, with a stop to see some petroglyphs. Saw some cool sights, as you can tell from the pace it's far from a thrill ride, but was a very laid back, casual ride down the Colorado, and our guide was excellent.
After that, it was a bus ride back with a 40 minute stop at a trading post.

A pretty laid back but enjoyable day. Everything was done well. If you're looking for more of a thrill just do one of the air tours, but if what I described sounds good then you'll enjoy this tour.

Review Title: See it all in one day!
Review Text: Spendy but worth it.  Traveled with 14, 17 and 18 yr olds. They loved it!  Not recommended for young children; too long of a day. Day started out with a 515am pick up from our hotel in the South Rim to the airport.  Airport clean, well organized and in tip top shape.  Pilots super professional.  Beautiful scenic East Rim flyover to Page watching the sun rise. Pick up from the airport to the Navajo Nation was in open air trucks...bring scarves and eye protection as it is super dusty (and COLD!!! Our trip was in mid-October).  Our Navajo guide Dee was amazing, knew all the nooks and crannies if the Canyon as well as all the proper camera techniques to get the best shots.  Then on to the rafting trip down the Colorado with the starting point at the Glen Canyon Dam @ Lake Powell.  Had to go thru security as the Dam is part of Homeland Security.  The rafting trip is pretty long (3+ hrs) have to admit was getting pretty antsy by the end...but BEYOND beautiful: saw petroglyphs, wild horses and big horn sheep.  Lunch was a Subway bag (turkey sandwich loaded w veggies, chips, fruit and a kind bar).  Picked up at the end of the rafting trip by a clean modern bus that did a midway pitstop at the trading post in Cameron.  All guides were professional, knowledgeable  and passionate about the area.  Coordination between legs of the trip involved some waiting but overall seemless.  If you only have one day to see Northern AZ/Glen Canyon this is the way to do it!

Review Text:
Wow! Is what comes to mind when thinking about the experience we had with Grand Canyon Landmarks Tour by Airplane. Despite a very windy day, our pilot decided it was safe enough to take us up and informed us that our flight would be rocky, but still safe. Safe was all I needed to hear.

The 45 minute flight was a tour of the entire South Rim and included an on-flight informative guide (via headphones) that turned out to be very insightful.

Finding parking at the Grand Canyon airport was fairly easy and so was our check in. I would highly recommend bringing your own camera to take pictures of what will probably be the best vantage point into the canyon. I would also try my best to board the plane first. Although everyone will get a window seat, (on a smaller plane; 8-10 people) there are a few seats that have a wing blocking your shot, thus preventing you from capturing the perfect picture. If you are simply there to take in the sights, any seat will be fine.

If you are prone to motion sickness, I would recommend bringing gum, or taking something for it before your flight departs. Keep in mind that if it is too windy and deemed unsafe your flight may be cancelled (check the weather). However, if there are high winds and it's safe to go, it will feel like a 45 minute roller-coaster ride.

I am very pleased with this experience and would definitely do it again. The ticket price is well worth it and I am very thankful that our pilot turned out to be happy and experienced and landed us safely.

Review Title: A full Day by AIR, LAND, RIVER & BUS!
Review Text: We wanted to see as much as possible with little time so we paid the extra $ to do this deluxe tour.  It started at the Grand Canyon airport and we promptly arrived at 6:00 a.m. Unfortunately, a party of 12 decided they wanted to also join the tour so we had to wait until they were all registered even tho we had made prior arrangements & had paid in full weeks before.  The receptionist was not at all engaging & would not allow us to at least get our breakfast until all 12 members were weighed & ticketed.  Very frustrating & a bit underwhelmed especially since we had arranged to be there on time by getting a room close by.  The pilot was good but it would have been nice had he introduced himself.  I did ask him his name.  But to me, I would prefer he introduce himself before we began.  The flight was nice & we saw the Grand Canyon from a mile above.  It was amazing. The Colorado river looks small from way up there. Later we arrived in Page, AZ & were picked up by Rosie, an American Indian tour guide who drove us to Antelope Canyon!  She was very nice, fun, engaging, helpful in showing us how to get the best pictures, & extremely professional & pleasant. She dropped us off at the River check in destination where we received lunch (Subway sandwiches & trimmings) along with a chance to clean up, use the facilities, learn about the Glen Canyon Dam, early explorers, etc.  Then we were bussed to a very long tunnel which we entered, pitch dark for about a minute or two, it was long & arrived at the opening of the stairs down to the river rafts.  Our guide was Daniel & he was very nice, engaging, professional, fun & made every effort to keep us cool on a very hot hot day.  We, about 16 of us on the boat, ate our lunch & listen to Daniel's talk about the river as well as the cliffs, petroglyphs, etc.  There was a couple of stops along the way which were welcomed along with a bathroom that was actually very clean and pleasant considering there actually large & basically out-houses. There was also an opportunity to swim and play in the very cold river, which was very refreshing. We finally made our way to the landing where we had another rest break before hopping on a very nice air conditioned plush seat bus (w/ a bathroom on board) to make the 3 hour journey back to the airport in Tusayan.  We saw extremely large Elk with huge racks & also babies and Does.  The driver was very nice, engaging & gave us lots of history & pertinent information. We liked the stop at  Cameron too!

Review Text: We opted for a 45 minute flight in a Twin Otter Vistaliner to see more of the GC instead of going on the Skywalk.  It cost a little more but was sure worth it.  At check in, be prepared to be weighed and then you are assigned a seat based upon weight and balance. You are assigned a colour coded boarding pass and wait until your flight is called.  You then stand in your assigned place indicated by painted footprints on the ground at the gate.  When it is safe to do so, you will be escorted to your plane and a professional photographer will offer to take your picture.  After a safety briefing and boarding is complete you can don your headphones and choose your language for the commentary.  Although the plane can hold 19 passengers, there is a very good chance you will be seated next to a window.  The flight itself was superb with spectacular views of the GC from another angle and there are many photo opportunities on either side of the plane through the large windows.  You also get to see some of the Northern Rim, something that is not easy to do in one day if travelling by road.  The flight does cross over the Canyon itself twice so it is possible to look straight down on the Colorado River and see the white water rafters doing their thing.  A lot of consideration is given to not disturbing the peace of those on the ground but this does not mean that the route flown is out of the way.   Highly recommended.

Review Title: Highlight of our entire trip to the Grand Canyon
Review Text: We booked a private Ecostar Imperial helicopter tour for 6 people (the 40-50 minute flight from Grand Canyon airport in Tusayan) and we are all in agreement that this was by far the highlight of our entire trip! We checked in 30 minutes before our flight and were all weighed to distribute our weight in the helicopter evenly. We all had a good view from the big windows in the Ecostar, even the two who were in the back/middle (2 people sit next to the pilot up front, and 4 in the back), although this was probably easier because we were a family group without issues leaning over each other or asking each people closer to a window to take a photo. The weather was perfect, with little cloud cover - we chose a morning flight because we heard the light is nice and there are fewer updrafts from the hot canyon floor, making for a smoother ride, and both points were true. The pilot was excellent (Tim) and told us about various sites as we passed them and answered our questions. It was magical flying over the Kaibab forest and hitting the rim of the canyon. This was my 4th trip to the Grand Canyon but my first helicopter trip, and it was definitely an experience entirely different from walking along both rims and hiking to the base of the canyon, with panoramic views above inaccessible viewpoints. We loved seeing the full range of the Colorado River, the confluence of the Little and main Colorado River, with the color change of the water, Imperial Point at the North Rim, the view of the canyon of the North Rim without the 4.5 hour drive from the South Rim, and the Dragon Corridor. It was certainly a pricey experience, but all of us felt that it was worth every penny and we would do it again if we ever returned to the Grand Canyon!

Review Text: This flight (7:00 - 8:00 am) was actually the first of 3 separate activities packaged together by Grand Canyon Scenic Airlines (Papillion Air) into a fantastic 11 1/2 hour thrilling day adventure ($399 per person total, and worth it).  Weather and crowds make all the difference. We had the first beautiful day in a week (others, our pilot said, were largely obscured by low clouds inside the canyon). Flight is over (not in) the Canyon, including great views of Grand Coulee Dam and Lake Powell before landing in Prescott by the Navajo Nation.  We paid $15 each extra for a guaranteed window seat—but unnecessary because we had only 11passengers and each had a window (24 passenger aircraft).  And most of them we learned were not part of our full day (their loss).    Crowds? Not in the plane. And this was the last two weeks of many seasonal tours, so none all day.      Second part was a gentle 1.5 mile Jeep Drive with an excellent, entertaining Navajo driver, our guide,to their Antelope Canyon.  A walking narrow slot canyon with other-worldly wind and water carved passages often so narrow you can touch both sides. Check google for some pictures. About 2 hours total.    Third, a 45 min. bus ride to Grand Coulee ending through a long tunnel ~8 mins) through the cliff side, down to the Colorado River as it exits base of the dam.  Boarded a motorized semi- rigid raft (actually aluminum, not an inflatable Avon) with 15 others. Started a 5 hour float, no rapids or white water, just spectacular views everywhere.  One stop, a picnic ground with toilets and 1/3 mile walk to petroglyphs on the low wall; and Subway box lunch provided.   Float ended at Lees Ferry, where we saw rafting groups starting out on 3-day runs through the rugged deep canyon river we all associate with Powell’s expedition.   From there a 2 hour bus ride back to our GC Airport start. That sounds boring, but not!    The bus driver, like our river guide, was entertaining and full of information all the way.  Driving into the park at late  sunset lots of elk were active, too.    DO NOT just settle for the fly over.

Review Title: Beautiful views of the Grand Canyon
Review Text: We took the 45 minute flight over the Grand Canyon. The terminal was easy to locate, the check in process was efficient and the waiting area comfortable. We had expected to be on a Twin Otter aircraft but instead flew on a Cessna Grand Caravan an 8 seat single engine aircraft. Our pilot was friendly and competent, and I felt at all times that we were under the care of a professional. The interior of the Caravan is a bit small but even at 6'7" I was able to fit relatively comfortable in the seat though I did have to crane my neck a bit to see out the window. The good news about this plane is every seat is a window seat and the windows are more than large enough to offer spectacular views of the Grand Canyon. The narration on the in flight head set was well done, and our pilot showed us some great views, even diverting a bit to give us a look at a heard of buffalo on the North Rim. The flight lived up to expectations as we saw all the points of interest they advertised and had some truly unique views you can't get from either rim. Do not expect this to be like a ride in a commercial jet, due to thermals and high winds the plane tends to get bounced around a lot, with plenty of ups and downs, with that being said our pilot was always in control and kept us right on course the whole flight. I would definitely recommend this tour, just don't eat a heavy meal before boarding.

Review Title: Amazing trip to the Grand Canyon
Review Text: We wanted to visit the Grand Canyon from Las Vegas and chose the Connoisseur trip offered by Grand Canyon Scenic Airlines. We didn’t fancy a lengthy bus trip, so chose this option as it involved a 30 minute bus from our Vegas hotel to Boulder City airport and a 1 hour flight to the Grand Canyon airport at the South Rim. Not only was the flight quicker but we got some great views on the way flying over the Hoover Dam, Lake Mead and some of the Canyon. We then transferred to a bus where our excellent driver and guide Steve took us to two different viewpoints - Bright Angel and Mathers Point where we spent about an hour at each. We would have loved longer to absorb the amazing views, but it still gave us enough time to enjoy it. Overall spending about 3 hours at the Canyon is probably longer than the average tour coming from Vegas. The flight in terms of view and reduced travel time was worth the extra cost. Not cheap for a family of four but well worth it.

Review Title: Action packed adventure at the Grand Canyon
Review Text: Our family had a great time on the combination tour including a flight over the Grand Canyon, a walk through Antelope Canyon, and a float trip down the Colorado River.  The trip was not cheap, but it was worth every penny.  We packed everything we wanted to see in to one day.  I recommend getting a seat on the port (left) hand side of the aircraft for best pictures.  We arrived at Antelope Canyon early before the crowds started to arrive.  Our native guide as fantastic.  I recommend giving your phone or camera to the guide throughout the canyon and ask them to help you with pictures.  The float trip down the river was very calm with no rapids.  You will not get wet so you don't need a bathing suit, unless you want to go swimming.  The river is only 50 degrees so it is not for the faint of heart.  Don't forget a hat, sunglasses, sunscreen, and lots of water.  It's hot out there.  Enjoy!

Review Title: Used them before, and would again
Review Text:
On a previous trip to Vegas we've used this excellent company to visit the Grand Canyon, so we booked with them again as my son-in-law hadn't seen it.
We weren't disappointed. As confirmed the previous day by telephone, the pick-up was prompt, the trip to the airport outside Vegas swift and smooth, and a very pleasant wait for our flight at a fascinating little airport, watching the planes and choppers depart and arrive.
My pregnant daughter - who isn't a good traveller anyway - wasn't sick on the flight, which showed how smooth it was. We got great views of Lake Mead, the Hoover Dam, and the Grand Canyon as we came into Tusayon Airport. My daughter was a little sick after the landing, but soon recovered,
We viewed the safety video and boarded our chopper without too much delay, and the staff were brilliant - attentive and caring. Read the company timeline on the wall while you wait, it's fascinating.
The flight over the canyon was amazing, and the audio commentary was supplemented by interesting and insightful comments from our pilot.
We returned to the airfield and were met by our driver, Eric, who drove us to Mather point for an hour's viewing, and then around the park a little, giving us interesting historical and personal facts about the area. He was really friendly, polite and pleasant to know.
The airplane flight back to Vegas was rougher than the trip in due to afternoon thermals, but all the passengers slept, apart from my son-in-law, who was rewarded with even better views of the canyon than on the flight in.
My daughter benefitted from sleeping, as she wasn't ill at all.
All the drivers, staff and pilots were fantastic, as were the aircraft - Twin Otter with HUGE viewing windows, choppers with larger than normal viewing windows and specially developed whisper jet engines and quiet rotors.
Brilliant!

Review Title: This was a great day trip!
Review Text:
This was a great day! I do have a few suggestions to improve it.

The airplane trip over the Grand Canyon started very early. The box breakfast before the plane ride was nice. I would suggest saying the fruit and granola bar for later because no snack or water will be offered you until the boat ride. The plane was small but comfortable. The plane had seen better days. There was still trash in the seat pockets from the last riders. Also, my headphones did not work to hear the recorded audio tour. I had to reach to the seat in front of me to get headphones that worked. If the plane had been full, I would not have been able to hear the recording. The recording was boring. Fortunately, the pilot gave a smooth ride and landing. The scenery was, of course, spectacular.

After, the plan ride we were dumped in a very small airport and loaded into jeeps for a tour of the antelope canyon. The tour of the antelope canyon was really beautiful. The guide was knowledgeable and friendly. She had lots of good photographic tips.

Between the plane ride and antelope tour, there was no offer of snacks or drinks. It was a very long morning between the box breakfast and getting on the boat.

At the raft headquarters, we were rudely pointed to some outhouses which did not have any toilet paper and were in bad need of being emptied. The way we were treated at this part of the tour almost ruined the day for me. We were handed our lunches and sent for a bag search. I'm not sure why we were handed our lunches at this point. It would make more sense to have the lunches at the boats already on board.

The bus ride to the boat was extremely rough in the old school bus which needed shocks..

The boat ride down Glen Canyon was spectacular! Our guide, Jarod, was charming, entertaining, knowledgeable, and thoughtful. This was a great part of the tour. We stopped a couple of times to stretch legs and use the restrooms. (The restrooms in the canyon were better than the restrooms at the rafting headquarters.) There was water and lemonaid offered on the boat.

We were not prepared for the loooonnnnnggg bus ride, 2 1/2 hours, back to the airport. We stopped at a trading post which was very nice. I would have liked to have a stop at a canyon overlook during this long ride back. Then, the day could have included a view of the canyon from the sky, river, and edge.

Overall, really a great day, however, the trip organizers need to be more considerate of the comfort of their patrons.

Review Title: Scenic Tour of Grand Canyon, Antelope Canyon and Colorado River all in one day!!
Review Text: Our family of 4 booked this trip due to limited time during our vacation to see the Grand Canyon.  I thought it would the perfect solution and sounded like fun.  I have two girls, 20 and 14. We all enjoyed the short plane ride over the Grand Canyon once we made it to the airport.  We received our box breakfast, which consisted of an apple, yogurt, muffin and a small orange juice.  Not too bad.  Got to Page AZ where they escorted us into the airport office to await our "jeep" ride to Antelope Canyon.  Well they loaded us in the back of a trailer attached to a pick up truck.  It was Memorial Day, and not quite warm enough for a 15 minute trip in an open trailer on the back of a truck but we made it.  Our tour guide was Rosie.  Very nice and knowledgeable about the Canyon.  It was amazing and a pleasant surprise for our tour.  Pictures we got were phenomenal.  Spent about 1-2 hours here.  It was hot once we got to Antelope Canyon but the temp inside was cool.  When this part of the tour was done, they loaded us again in the trailer and took us to the drop for the raft portion of the trip. It was around 12 noon now.  They gave us our box lunches that were decent; ham sandwich, chips, granola bar, apple and a cookie.  We got to the boat part and they once again loaded us on school bus and we road to a loading area near a dam.  I believe it was called Glen Canyon Dam.  It looks very similar to Hoover Dam and to see it close up was kinda cool.  They split the families up and escorted us to these large pontoon rafts like shown in the online pictures.  They are nice.  They are stocked with cans of lemonade and a big jug of water so you can refill your water bottles.  We did this several times due to the length of the trip and the heat.  Keep in mind it was only May 28th and temps were around 85-90 that day in the Canyon.  They raft ride was beautiful but a little too long.  We were on the boat for about 5 hours.  Could have done it 3 and that would have been enough for us all.  The scenery was beautiful, we stopped a couple of times to see different sights.  We put our feet in the Colorado River which was about 47 degrees.  We got back to the dock and they escorted us to a large motor coach for the 3 hours ride back to the Airport.  EVERYONE on the bus was exhausted.  I think everyone, including kids went to sleep.  That bus was as quite as a church.  We road about 1-1/2 hours and we stopped at a gift shop.  You could go to the restroom, get a snack or buy souvenirs.  We then drove to the Grand Canyon National Park to drop those who were staying there.  They took the rest of us to the airport right after.  We got back to our car around 6 I believe.  LONG day.   LOTS of great memories and pictures.  Glad we did it.  Would be a much better tour if the raft portion was continuous movement and a shorter time frame.

Review Text:
My husband and children (18,19) had a great time on this trip! The early morning plane ride was terrific, and as we had read before, it’s best to sit on the left side of the plane for the best views!
The off road driving in trucks to Antelope Canyon was pretty bumpy and dusty- but hey- you’re on an adventure! Our guide Patrick was amazing; a native to the area and extremely knowledgeable about every camera and phone camera! Got us the best pictures! A wonderful guide!
The boxed lunches came next, pretty good- only no specific time to eat them. We were starving since we’d been going since 6am and so we ate them on the bus ride to the raft place (even though they said no eating on the bus!) after the informal TSA check. Our rafting guide, Jerod, was really terrific; super knowledgeable and kept all the younger kids on the boat engaged! The only thing I was disappointed in, was not wearing my bathing suit, as we had opportunity to get in the river, and I hadnt read it was going to be allowed. The rafting was super hot, but lemonade and water are provided, and he put the boat in the shady areas as much as possible when we were stationary hearing about the canyon.
The walk up to the ptyroglyphs is eh, well, a few carvings on rock- not that impressive- but history I understand. Nice comfy AC bus back. Stop at gift store Ok too! Overall we loved the whole trip!

Review Title: Air, Land and Water Tour. Poor Coordination and Management of Time.
Review Text:
We were really looking forward to the 'Scenic Canyon River Adventure' tour that was offered through Grand Canyon Scenic Airlines.

To take you through the process, let us start at the beginning:

You arrive at the airport, where you were promised a breakfast prior to your plane flight. The breakfast was a box breakfast, made up of a muffin, yogurt, apple and an orange juice. If you wanted coffee, you had better arrive early, because they only had one coffee dispenser, which emptied quickly, and they were not going to refill it.

Once on the plane, if you were fortunate enough to sit on the left side, you had spectacular views of the South and North Rims. However, if like me, you sat on the right, you only had views of the dry, flat land. Occasionally, you caught a glimpse of the canyon itself.

When we returned to the airport, we were told to step outside to wait to be picked up by a vehicle to take us to Antelope Canyon. A pickup truck showed up, rather than the hummers they displayed on their booking website!. They started shuffling people in the bed of the truck, where they had tight bench seating. The kept telling us to 'Hurry, Hurry'. They tried to separate me and my husband, and we said we together and did not want to be separated on the tour. The driver was incredibly rude, and told us that there was only room for one, and we imay not fit on the next truck coming through.

We took our chances and waited for the next vehicle. We got in that truck bed, and the truck raced away to a strip mall parking lot, where they were picking up additional people for the tour, who were running late. They yelled at the people to 'Hurry, Hurry, Hurry...you are making everyone late!'

When everyone was finally on board, the truck sped through streets and then on to a rough dirt road, where we were jostled and choking down dust and dirt from the road.

We finally arrived at Antelope Canyon, our tour guide led us through as a group. This, quite honestly, was the best part of our tour. The guide was amazing and knowledgeable. She even helped us align our cameras to get the best photo ops. She pointed out not only the rock formations and nicknames for the formations, but also had great historic stories of floods through the canyon. Very enjoyable!!!

Following this tour, we were loaded back in to the trucks and taken to a bus pickup location, where we were given some instructions on the raft portion of our tour, and handed box lunches. These consisted of a good turkey sandwich, chips, cookies and an apple.

We arrived at the raft launch, and boarded the raft. The guide on this tour spent much of the time talking about himself, but did manage to slip in a bit of history along the way. They did provide water and lemonade on the raft to keep everyone hydrated. This turned out to be a good thing, because it was not a 'fast' raft trip. Rather, most of the time, the raft sat stationary, while the guide talked and pointed out the rock formations and explained the reasons for the formations and colors.

Unfortunately, we were almost always just sitting in the sun, and without any movement, we didn't even have the brief relief of a breeze. The raft ride was drawn out well beyond what was necessary. Everyone on board was so relieved to get off of the raft! The trip could have been done in less than half the time, and move along at a better pace.

From there, we were place on a bus to take everyone back. The did drop some people off directly at their hotels/lodges, prior to taking everyone back to the airport where we started. Unfortunately, because everyone was on edge from the unnecessarily lengthy raft trip, people were very irritated that they had to wait to be taken back to the airport. Poor bus driver!

Overall, we would say to save your money, and not take this 'adventure' trip!!!

Review Text: I guess it depends on what you’re looking for, but I wanted to go to the Canyon and Hoover Dam whilst we were close by in Vegas. Review Text:
We were lucky enough to have this trip gifted to us by my sister as a thank you, after this trip we are the ones thanking her for such a great experience. Seeing the Grand Canyon in person is one thing you really need to do if you get the chance. But to see it from a low flying plane, getting to walk through a slot canyon then raft down the river from Glen Canyon is a truly memorable way to spend a full day.

We started the day at sunrise on a 9 seater plane taking off from Tusayan airport. We had a 30 minute flight over the canyon with the added excitement of some bad turbulence to wake everyone up. After landing we got in a jeep to the famous Antelope Canyon. We were given a great guided tour which included assistance on the best camera settings and vantage points to get the best photographs.

After that it was back on the jeep for a ride into the dam at the head of Glen Canyon. We then got on our rafts for a leisurely 2.5 hour float down the calm waters of Glen Canyon. Your sense of perspective is really fooled by the sheer scale of the canyon and the height of the walls towering above you. We got to float around horseshoe bend, stop for a picnic lunch, see ancient wall drawings and were even lucky enough to a see a family of horses drinking from the river edge near the end of the trip.

It was a truly wonderful day that won't be forgotten, we spent the next day driving along the south rim which was spectacular, but actually being down in the canyon was a special experience and something we highly recommend.

Review Title: Tolles Erlebnis zu Wasser, Luft und zu Land
Review Text:
Dieser Tagesausflug ist ein absolutes Highlight bei einem Besuch des Grand Canyons. Es geht sehr früh los mit einem Flug über den Grand Canyon mit tollen Eindrücken, vor allem wenn die Sonne gerade am Aufgehen ist. Horseshoe Bend von oben zu sehen und eigene Fotos zu schießen sind tausendmal besser als jede Postkarte.

Nach der Landung in Page wurden wir zum Antelope Canyon gebracht und genossen eine eher hektische Führung mit Photo-mach-Hinweisen. Der Antelope Canyon ist einfach zu eindrucksvoll um noch ein paar Worte über die hektische Führerin zu verlieren.

Die Fahrt ab dem späten Vormittag auf dem Colorado River ist nicht minder beeindruckend. Der Unterschied zum Flug ist die Sicht nun nach oben. Die eindrucksvollen Steilwände wirken nicht eintönig und wenn man dann beim Horseshoe Bend vorbeikommt, diesmal aber unten, werden die Dimensionen noch einmal vor Augen geführt. Der Bootsführer untermalte mehr oder weniger zu jeden Stein mit einer persönlichen Story, aber man muß ja nicht immer zuhören.

Der letzte Teil der Tour geht dann mit dem Bus zurück nach Tusayan. Der Fahrer weiß natürlich auch einiges zu erzählen und der obligatorische Stop an einer Trading Post lockert das ganze auf.

Der Tagesausflug war ein sehr tolles Erlebnis. Wer nicht so lange Zeit hat am Grand Canyon zu bleiben, sollte so etwas machen. Es ist auf jeden Fall ein Erlebnis und auch wenn es lange dauert, so schöne Eindrücke von oben und von unten des Colorado Rivers und der Canyons bekommt man anders nur sehr schwer.

Review Title: Det koster, men det er alle pengene værd
Review Text:
Hvis man skal til Grand Canyon National Park, bør man overveje at investere i en helikoptertur. Det koster en del, men det er det hele værd.
Der er flere udbydere, men Papillon kan bestemt anbefales.
Her er der topprofessionelle folk, der går meget op i, at det skal være en helstøbt oplevelse. Vi oplevede, at alle medarbejdere var utrolig service-mindede og høflige, og manden, der skulle hjælpe til med boarding forstod endda at joke med os gæster.
Vi blev vist hen til en af de mange helikoptere og hilste på vores venlige pilot. Han fortalte sikkert en del interessante ting undervejs, men jeg må indrømme, at når man først flyver ud over kløften - akkompagneret af temaet fra Jurassic Park i headsettet - hører man ikke meget efter.
Vores tur varede desværre kun en lille halv time, men til gengæld fik vi en oplevelse for livet.

Review Title: I love the Colorado River - its an amazing place to visit a must do!
Review Text: We were in Las Vegas and the 3 of decided we wanted to do a bit of local nature. After looking at all the options we selected to do a raft tour on the Colorado River, we booked via Viator and the vendor was on time at 815am to pick us up and start the journey below the Hoover Dam, it took a while to get there, but eventually we boarded the raft and off we went.  It’s an amazing river, the water is clean 98% for drinking and at some points its 30 feet deep. You know you in Nature floating down the river and looking at the rocky banks with some small “beaches” you can stop for swimming when the water is not below 50 degrees.  We enjoyed every moment of our 3 hour journey.  The lunch they offered sucked, we were starving by the time we got back to Vegas LOL.  The trip ends on the Arizona side where the clock/time never changes…weird and funny at the same time, two states separated by a river having different time zones.  A must do!  Next time we want to rent canoes and do it on our own.

Review Title: This is a good way to see the canyon from a new perspective
Review Text:
The on line reservation process was pretty easy.
The location is relatively easy to find.

The check in was easy and they allowed us to change flight time when our plans changed.
There is a waiting area, but on popular days it can be crowded.
The operation seemed to be well run. Pilots would come and call each group to the plane. No one was allowed on the flight line unescorted.

We were on the Caravan, which is a somewhat smaller plane which seated 10 people. The seats were not standard airline seats, but they were comfortable enough for a short flight. Some seats would be tight for very tall folks. The views were generally good, but some very tall or very short people might find some seats to have less than ideal views.
Each seat had Bose headphones. They played a prerecorded commentary which told a bit about the canyon and how it was formed. Occasionally the pilot would come on and add a bit of commentary.
I am a licensed pilot and to my eye, the aircraft appeared to be well maintained. The pilots appeared to be very competent and took safety very seriously.
The flight doesn’t go over the same part of the canyon as the visitor center, rather it appears the flights follow a set route to avoid the popular areas.

The tour is not cheap at $150 or so, but it is cheaper than the helicopter tours and it allows you to see a great deal of the canyon from a perspective you can only get from the air.
I would recommend this tour.

Review Text:
I travelled with my family (3 of us) and had one full day to get to know the Grand Canyon in the most comprehensive way possible. We spent the prevoius late afternoon at the South Rim. After some research we came upon this tour. What a best way to spend a full day at the Grand Canyon than by air, land and river? The tour is expensive indeed, but worth it, specially if you have children. The three parts of the tour are led by very professional people. Oue pilots, Antelope Canyon Navajo guide and our river guide were all awesome.

Your day starts at 6 am at the Grand Canyon airport located in Tusayan. After checking in and geting a decent boxed breakfast you climb over the canyon with a group of no more than 20 people in a specially conditioned plane. Having viiews of the cnayon all the way to Page airport for an hour during the first light of the day is just incredible. Mind you...winds can pick up up there and you may have a bit of a bumpy ride for moments of the flight.

Next, after landing in Page, trucks will take you to Antelope Canyon early enough to beat the crowds (believe me, it makes a difference). Our guide was super and make magic with our phone cameras.

After that you are dropped off to pick up a packed lunch and get down to the river where you will raft for a few hours with a superb explanation of the formations, stop for a break, see petrogyphs, even swim in Colordao River if you want.

The vews from the river and the peace down there cannot be explained with words. It is a unique experience.

Later in the afternoon you have a 2 hour bus drive to Tusayan with a stop at Cameron Trading Post.

Review Title: Good airline to charter for your Grand Canyon float trip.
Review Text: Our group (Tour West) chartered with Grand Canyon Airlines to fly our group from Boulder City to Marble Canyon for the put-in, and then we were picked up at the Bar Ten Ranch airstrip at the conclusion of our river trip.  Our group of 16 flew in a Twin Otter, and the flights were professionally operated by experienced pilots.  There was quite a bit of wind shear flying into Marble Canyon so we were diverted to Page to land on the larger strip.  The pilot landed the aircraft in a serious cross-wind but he landed the plane safely.  Our flights were also very scenic by the way!  We fly a lot in Alaska in some pretty marginal weather, and I would recommend this airline to anyone visiting the Grand Canyon.

Review Title: Expected more of the Connoisseur tour
Review Text:
My husband and i booked our Connoisseur tour to go to the Grand Canyon South on the 19th and below is are overall experience:
Pros:
- Beautiful views as promised
- Very friendly staff - the bus driver at the Grand Canyon South was amazing! He blew us all away with his happiness, assisted us with answers and took amazing pictures of us and people on the tour with us.
Cons:
- The flight was delayed. Upon my complain they gave me a picture for free, but still sucks as you make plans for the day arrive there way earlier and have to wait an hour because the pilot is in training.
- The flight on our way there was AWFUL! We all thought we would not make it. The win was extremely strong, which I understand its not their fault. We were informed that we could face some turbulence and even signed a document for that, but that was not SOME that was the WHOLE flight which made us all very sick and because of that we were not able to enjoy the tour as much. So I wish the staff would have informed us of the extremely bad winds and offered to possibly reschedule the flight or something.
- The food they give us is not Connoisseur... it was just okay. So bring some snacks just in case.
- The last big complain was the windows. They were not as big as i saw in the pictures and expected. So maybe they flew us in another plane that had small windows which i did not like it at all especially with my husband being 6.4.

With all that said it is a good company, we might have just chosen a bad day.

Review Title: Bel tour, volo la scelta migliore
Review Text:
GRAND CANYON CONNOISSEUR (Papillon - Scenic Airlines)
Volo + pullman al South Rim
Piano di viaggio:
7.40 navetta hotel
8 cambio navetta alla stazione navette e partenza per aeroporto Boulder City
9.15 partenza volo da Boulder City
10.15 atterraggio aeroporto South Rim
11 arrivo con pullman a Gran Canyon Village (Bright Angel Lodge)
12.30 dopo visita autonoma, partenza per Mather Point
13 dopo visita autonoma, partenza per aeroporto South Rim
13.30 arrivo in aeroporto
14 decollo volo
15 atterraggio volo a Boulder City
15.30 navetta per Las Vegas
16.30 navetta per hotel
16.35 arrivo hotel
Commento:
Per circa 300$, volo con aereo+autobus con 2 soste è forse la soluzione migliore per chi vuole visitare in giornata il Gran Canyon partendo e tornando a Las Vegas.
Il South Rim è forse una delle zone più spettacolari del Gran Canyon.
Le navette della Papillon ti vengono a prendere di fronte ai maggiori hotel della Strip. Con il volo (è un aereo da turismo, si vola relativamente bassi) si può ammirare il Canyon dall'alto e fare fotografie spettacolari (risparmiando sull'elicottero), oltre ad essere un mezzo veloce.
Sull'aereo c'è il commento in inglese, spagnolo e giapponese. Buona idea pagare i 15$ per il posto vicino al finestrino, per fare le foto dall'alto alla Diga di Hoover e al fiume Colorado.
Consiglio di scegliere un tour, come il Connoisseur, in cui si scende a terra, per immergersi veramente e percepire la grandezza del posto (sconsiglio i tour solo aerei). Le due soste dell'autobus Papillon sono sufficienti, il Canyon è simile nei vari punti.
Papillon professionale: quel giorno pioveva al mattino (rarissimo) e offrivano il rimborso a chi rinunciasse a partire, con riaccompagnamento a Las Vegas.
Viene fornito un pranzo con panino, 2 pacchetti di patatine, dolce e due bottigliette d'acqua a testa.
Prezzo non economico, ma è l'opzione migliore, sul pullman sarebbe stato un viaggio eterno, con l'elicottero si spendeva inutilmente troppo. Consigliatissimo.

Review Text: We took the plane ride from Tusayan up to Page, followed by a visit to Antelope Canyon and finally a float trip down the Colorado River from Glenn Canyon Dam down to Lee's Ferry.  Final stage was a bus trip back to Tusayan.  All of the guides were very knowledgeable and professional.  Pilot did a great job of showing us all of the canyon despite low cloud cover.  Antelope Canyon guide was excellent at pointing out the best photo ops, and even showed people how to get the most out of their I Phone cameras by having them select the proper settings in the different light conditions.  River guide (Justin) did a great job of explaining the canyon and the geology.  Also had some fun along the way with the other boats.  Bus ride back was very comfortable, with a nice movie about the history of white water rafting through the canyon.  The driver was very courteous and professional.  Outing was a full day and well worth it.

Review Text:
Selected "Grand Canyon Connoisseur" tour after seeing the great reviews here and was really looking forward to it.

Got off to a bad start as we had to wait an hour for the plane which was due to fly 9.15am (for the south rim) and there were no information/explanation whatsoever for the delay. Then the headphones on the plane was faulty.

Next, we were grouped together with a Japanese tour group, with a scenic airlines guide who appeared to be dedicated to them. From the minute we landed in Grand Canyon, there were no instructions on where to head to and we had to find our own way and ask around. On the coach rides, other than a short introduction from the other English speaking guide, the Japanese guide hogged the microphone and everything conversed during the rides were in Japanese language. This was despite there were other English speaking people on the tour, who obviously doesn't understand Japanese.

For each of the 2 stops, 50 minutes were given for us to walk around. The tour ended around 2pm and then AGAIN, another long 50 minutes wait for the return flight with no information on delay. Would have thought there would be better planning and more seamless transfers for an established tour.

Though the views of the Grand Canyon were fantastic, this tour really marred the whole experience.

Review Title: A must do day tour of the Grand Canyon & surrounds
Review Text: This was a 12 hour adventure to remember - it started with a flight over the Grand Canyon to Page, Arizona where we were then taken to the amazing slot canyons of Antelope Canyon via 4WD where our Native American guide took us through the slot canyons, giving us some helpful hints on achieving the perfect photos.  Then back to Page; handed our lunch packs and on a bus to join Colorado River Discovery on the mighty Colorado - don't panic, it was a motor driven raft, no rapids, 15.5 miles floating down the river...  you even get to float through Horseshoe Bend.... Make sure you swim, no matter how cold the water is.  Stopped for viewing of ancient petroglyphs; bathrooms along the way; lunch, snacks and drinks.  Finish at Lee's Ferry, then board the bus for a 3.5 hour drive back to the airport; stopping for food or souvenirs at the Cameron Trading Post.

Review Text:

Découvrir le plateau et la forêt ainsi que les immenses crevasses le long du Colorado est une expérience à part.
Il faut réserver à l'avance et y aller en début de matinée ou en fin d'après-midi pour avoir une belle luminosité pas trop agressive.
L'avion dispose de grande baies vitrées qui permettent de faire des photos et surtout d'apprécier le paysage.
Des casques audio filtrent le bruit et délivrent des commentaires traduits en plusieurs langues.
Seul bémol, ça secoue pas mal, surtout à l'arrière, j'étais un brin malade à la fin ^^

Review Text:
This should have been one of the highlights of our trip. We booked well in advance and purposely selected Gran Canyon Airlines as they advertised "the largest flat, un-tinted panoramic windows on any air tour aircraft, perfect for sightseeing and photography!". Being a keen photographer, I wanted to ensure that I was able to take as many pictures as possible. Unfortunately, GCA are not true to their word and offered an alternate aircraft to the Vista Liner (Cessena Caravan) that has small tinted windows (blue tint) effectively ensuring all pictures are throw away. Once I had realised that we had been placed on an alternate aircraft, not ideal for photography I requested that we change to a different flight. Not interested, the team at the counter would just not accommodate. Their response was, "You are better off in the Caravan as they don't smell of oil, the Vista Liners stink of oil from the engines"... The trip is fantastic and it really is an experience that you will never forget, such a shame I have a set of blue pictures to remember the day.

Tip; ensure that you are booked on the, as advertised, Vista Liner with a window seat if you want to take decent photos.

Review Text:
We arrived early for our pre booked flight. This was not a problem and we were put on to an earlier flight. The reception area has a gift shop check in area and waiting area and restrooms.
You are given a color coded ticket at check in and the pilots come out and call the color and you line up ready to walk out to you aircraft. In our case we were yellow and there were 8 of us who lined up. We were guided to our Cessna Caravan by the pilot . This is a small aircraft and can be bumpy so don't overdo your breakfast!!!!. Before boarding we had an official photo taken and then boarded this small aircraft. After being strapped in everyone had a window seat my husband and I had the front row right behind the pilot what a view.! After safety instructions and putting our earphones on which you then choose your language we started to taxi down the runway. I have never been on this small an aircraft and was very nervous but wow I am so pleased I have done it, what an amazing experience and the views over the Grand Canyon are awesome. It was a little bumpy at times as it was windy but we new this would the case. The flight took 45 minutes and we saw the south rim and the north rim of the canyon.
After the flight we were able to purchase the official photo.
If you want to use the helicopter service this operates from the same place. They also have a twin otter aircraft which is larger than our Cessna .
I would highly recommend this company to take you on this awesome experience of a lifetime.

Review Text:
I visited the Grand Canyon in March-it is still a bit chilly-bring your layers! I highly recommend this tour. Here is a bit of what to expect on this tour.

I had to be at the airport at 6:30 am for check-in. Be sure to go to the airport, not the heliport with the helicopters. I was given a box with my breakfast-a muffin, apple, yogurt, and trial mix, and there was coffee available. They weighed me and my bag, and advised me not to bring any knives or weapons on board. We boarded a little after 7 am and we were in a small prop plane, there were three seats across and about 7 rows. Headphones were used to give the audio tour, and there is a choice of language but everyone on my tour used English. I am unsure of what the other language choices were. We took off and were soon flying over the Grand Canyon. My window seat was amazing! It's a great way to see the canyon. unforgettable! Then we flew over Glen Canyon, and over Horseshoe bend, then the dam and then landed in Page AZ airport. We then directly got into the tour jeeps for the Antelope Canyon Tour. Be advised, these jeeps are very bumpy!! Sitting in the back of essentially a cage with two benches welded on the back of a crew cab pickup. If you have back or neck issues that could be flared by a bumpy ride, you could ask to sit up front with the driver in the crew cab. It didn't seem the safest way to drive first on a hiway and then on a dirt road, using a single lap belt to two passengers. but hey we did!

After the scary ride, we arrived at Antelope Canyon and we were the first tour group of the day. This makes for much better photo ops! The guide told us how to set our phones or camera and where to take photos. We really got some awesome photos and enjoyed the tour. Then back in the jeep and they took us to the river tour company for our river tour.

At the River raft tour company there is a coffee shop and some snacks. We got our sack lunches for the raft trip there. After a bag check to make sure we did not have any weapons (because in order to get to our raft, we had to go through a tunnel at the base of the dam that is controlled by Homeland Security) We took the bus to the base of Glen Canyon dam and go on our large rafts. You won't get wet to any extreme. You might get a little splash is all. It was cold in the shade and I wished I had more layers, but then when in the full sun it was a lot warmer. Again, wear layers!! The sack lunch is good, you can eat it ant any time. I had an apple, sandwich, trail mix, cookie, chips. There was lemonade and water on the raft. The raft trip was relaxing and awesome.

After the trip, we took a tour bus back to the airport with a stop at the Cameron Trading Post to shop for 30 minutes. Lots of cool Indian made gifts there. They dropped off the people staying at hotels in the park first followed by the Tusayan hotel and then back to the airport for those that had driven there. A very long day but totally awesome. Would do it again in a heartbeat.

Review Title: The absolute best Grand Canyon Tour
Review Text: If you have traveled to the Grand Canyon for seeing its beauty, splurge and take the 12 hour tour offered by Grand Canyon Airlines. About 1 hour of flight time over the Grand Canyon, Marble Canyon, and Glen Canyon to Page Arizona where you will be driven by Ford Trucks disguised as jeeps to a beautiful area of Antelope Canyon. Not much walking so most can go to see the beautiful slot canyon. The Indian guide was very knowledgeable about the area and in how to take the perfect photo. After this the same trucks take you to the river tour area where you are taken by bus to the Glen Canyon Dam. Here you board a large stable raft (again appropriate for most people, as long as you can climb one step). Take a breathtaking 3 hour raft ride through Glen Canyon. Bring your lunch, water is provided and don't forget sunscreen. If you like you can take a quick dip into the Colorado river at one or two spots on the river. The water is cold.

Review Text: We were hesitant to spend the money on the Grand Canyon Experience package but this was one of the most memorable and amazing ways to really see the Canyon.  Grand Canyon Airlines begins your journey with giving you breakfast and then having you board a small plane to fly you over the Grand Canyon and the Colorado River.  While on board you listen to a recording about the geological history of the area.  Next you land in Page where you are picked up in an open air jeep for an exciting dusty and bumpy off road journey through the desert to Antelope Canyon.  You disembark and the guide takes you through the Canyon and explains its history while pointing out and helping you set up to take photographers that look like something out of a book.  Our guide was an amazing photographer.  After your photo session, you are taken to The Colorado River Rafting Company in Page and are given a bag lunch.  They take you to Glenn Canyon Dam where you descend to the Colorado River and board a raft which will slowly take you down the river while your river guide explains the history of Lake Powell, the river, and the geology.  You stop along the river to eat lunch and explore the ancient cliff drawings.  A bus picks you up at Lees Ferry and takes you to a Native trading Post in Cameron where you can purchase souvenirs before heading back to Grand Canyon airport.  There is no better way to experience every aspect of this breathtaking area.

Review Text:

Received a call at 6:41am the day of the flight to say there was an hour delay, but unfortunately we were already on the way as our hotel was a 35 minutes drive away. No matter, we arrived at 7am knowing we were in for a 2 hour wait now that the flight was delayed till 9am.

Review Text:
We did the full day tour on our first full day at the Grand Canyon, and I couldn't think of a better way to see some of the amazing beauty of the area.

We started with the air tour over the Grand Canyon, which my daughters loved! It was so beautiful to see the sun rising over the canyon and we were really able to get a feel for it's vastness from the air. The flight was over way too soon - we would have loved to stay in the air and see more!!

Then we moved to the Antelope Canyon tour. Our tour guide was knowledgeable, and we were there early enough that there was only one other group there, so we got some really amazing photos. Be aware, you must walk through the canyon, and then come back the same way to get back to the vehicles. It was very crowded when we came back through and it would have been more convenient to have our ride waiting on the other end, but given the terrain the other side may not be accessible. The canyon itself was really beautiful, and seeing the swirls and marking from the water rushing through was very cool.

The final portion of our tour was the river rafting. It was very cool to raft through Glen Canyon, and see the inside of the canyon from the river view. The downside of this portion of the day was that while there was plenty of cold water (and we were frequently encouraged to stay hydrated) there was no shade on the raft at all, and the river water was really really cold. So cold that standing in it for more than a minute was painful. This made for a very hot afternoon. The river trip felt a little too long. It was fun and our guide was really great, but the heat was really starting to get to us. We stopped several times and the pace of the raft was very slow. Review Title: Wow! Canyon River Adventure was Amazing!
Review Text:
We had an amazing time on our June 9 Canyon River Adventure. From our morning arrival at the airport to our late-afternoon return, we were in awe by the views, activities, and services of this great adventure.

Flying over the Grand Canyon was breathtaking, and the flight crew did a great job pointing out what we were seeing. Additionally, there was a nice headset with music and some narration that kept interest and blocked "flight" noise often associated with smaller planes. There were about 20 of us on the plane and everyone had a great view, even from the middle seat, like me. Kudos to our pilots for a very smooth flight---including take-off and landing.

The tour continued to Antelope Canyon in Page, AZ. Our guide Colby was great. We were in a group of about 12 people. Great size group. In addition to the history of the canyon, he gave us tips on how to get the best photographs. Kids and adults loved it. Easy walk. Didn't need hiking shoes. We weren't sure what to expect.

Continued from there to gathering point with other groups to load up for ride to the Glen Canyon Dam and the Colorado River. Our smooth river ride with Brooke and Colorado River Discovery was great. She was a good boat captain, storyteller, historian, and entertainer. And the water was freezing, even in June. 47-degrees is the usual temperature. Splashing around felt good but you couldn't do it long.

Light breakfast and lunch were provided as well as water and lemonade. Definitely glad we had a couple water bottles to refill at the water stations along the way. Be sure to bring your cameras. Lots to photograph!!

And our ride back to Tusayan with Gigi on the bus was great. Got in a nap before our stop at the trading post in Cameron. The Navajo Taco she recommended was delicious. One fed our family of four. Least expensive meal of our week-long vacation. And delicious!!

Loads of fun for the whole family! Highly recommend even though it's a little pricey. Definitely worth it!

Review Title: A must do at the Grand Canyon!
Review Text:
We did the Scenic Canyon River Adventure today and it was amazing! It's a really long day (13 hours, start to finish) and not cheap, but it was completely worth it.
It started with our flight over the canyon on the way to Page, AZ. Craig was our pilot and he did a great job. They have a narration track you can listen to on the way which gives some of the history of the Grand Canyon and points out places of interest. The views are just spectacular and if you can only do the plane ride, do it!
Then, we were picked up after a short restroom break at the Page airport for our Antelope Canyon tour. Our driver/guide was really great and I really wish I could remember his name to mention here. Antelope Canyon is amazingly beautiful. We were there for around an hour, which was much longer than I expected, and had plenty of time to tour the entirety of Upper Antelope Canyon and take tons of photos. Our guide even showed everyone how to set up their cameras and the best spots to take photos.
We were then dropped off at Colorado River Discovery for our smooth water float trip. After about 30 minutes or so there to use the restroom, purchase snacks/souvenirs, we boarded a bus which took us to Glen Canyon Dam for our float trip. (They pass out your bagged lunch there before you get on the bus.) Make sure to let them know if you have any dietary restrictions when you make your reservation and they will accommodate you. We're vegetarian, and the veggie sandwich was pretty good (several slices of cheese, lettuce and tomato on whole grain bread, with various condiment packets in the lunch bag). Nate was our tour guide/captain for the float trip and he was fantastic! He was very knowledgeable and really seemed excited about taking us on this adventure. I will say, I agree with some other reviews on here that say that the float trip is a bit on the long side. There are a bunch of times when they cut the engine for you to get a look around you, but sometimes you're just drifting along for quite a while and you'd much rather have a breeze on your face and get on with it. It is VERY HOT and sunny on the raft, so make sure you take lots of water and reapply sunscreen a few times. A hat is a must! Also, if you plan to take a dip in the river when you stop at the halfway point, you might want to wear your bathing suit, but the water is about 47 degrees even at the beginning of June. There are two restroom breaks on the float trip, which is nice. In all, it was about 3.5 hours (including the two stops). I would have been happier with a brisker 2 hour tour.
Once the float trip is finished, you are picked up by bus at Lee's Ferry, after another short restroom break. Then it's 1.5 hours to Cameron Trading Post on the Navajo Reservation. You get 30 minutes to use the restroom, purchase snacks or souvenirs. Then, it's back on the bus for another 1.5 to 2 hours (depending on where you're being dropped off). Our bus driver, Gigi, was really friendly and had some interesting stories for us. The drive was long, but considering how far we flew out there, it's not that surprising.
All in all, it was a great day and we'd highly recommend it!

Review Text:
My ten year old daughter and I chose the Indian adventure tour and it was the best part of our entire vacation. We got picked up from circus circus at 4:30am by a very nice shuttle driver and taken around to pick up other guests before getting put on a large bus to the airport. At the airport we got weighed, got a colored sticker and waited for our flight. Fifteen minutes later we were on our cute little plane. The pilots were very nice and the plane has huge Windows. We were given a headset to listen to information about the landmarks along the way. A very short and smooth 30 minutes later and we arrived.
At the airport they give you a bracelet with a specific time written on it so you know what time to catch a shuttle back to the airport. All of the shuttle drivers were very friendly and the busses run quite often. The view from eagle point was spectacular. We didn't bother doing the skywalk because it's over priced and the view is just as good from the ground. We took the short hike at guano point and loved it as well. When we got done hiking we had a nice lunch next to the canyon at 9am. We had been up since 3:45 so lunch at 9 was just fine for us! The airline will tell you not to go to the western town at the ranch because you won't have time but we did. We had plenty of time to check out the horses and shoot a bow and arrow. We even had time to go back to eagle point one last time before going to the airport. After arriving back at Boulder city airport we hopped on a bus and were taken back to the hotel. We got back in our room at 1:30.
Overall, it was well worth every penny we spent and I would love to do it again. The only part we didn't love was the very long wait while other guests were dropped off at their hotel- we were the very last stop. Otherwise it was a perfect trip. Even the souvenirs aren't horribly over priced.
The only thing to keep in mind when traveling with young kids on this trip is there aren't any guard rails- none. So be very careful to keep them right next to you.
