Review Text:
We bought the Grand Canyon connoisseur through Scenic airlines, and in brief were not very satisfied with our trip, especially considering the cost.
For 300$ USD pp, we expected better service, better food, and better quality guide/tour information.
The day started with a very early pick up, at 715am from our Vegas hotel. After a lengthy drive to the boulder airport where we had breakfast, we were ready to fly. Our planned flight departure of 915 was delayed for unclear reasons until 10am. The flight was nice with impressive views down below, but very little information given. The headphones talk a little bit about Boulder City, Hoover Dam, and Mojave desert, but nothing about the Grand Canyon itself. The pilots don't say anything during the flight.

Once we landed, we are herded onto a small tour bus where our driver just yelled, didn't use the microphone system. It was difficult to hear and chat with him. We saw 2 stop off points, and again no real tour or information, just being dropped off with instructions to return within one hour.

We were expecting more knowledge/information about the beautiful Canyon, instead we were just dropped off without too much instruction. Again, for the cost and the way the website describes the tour, we expected much more. The boxed lunch is probably most representative of the quality of the tour. The website says you'll savour lunch.. it was a sandwich that everyone in our party of 6 couldn't finish, chips and cookies. No drink, but the driver did have mini bottles of water.
Returning to the bus, we were told a little bit about the local birds at the Canyon before returning to the airport and flying home. The sound system didn't even work on the way home and pilots were silent, so no additional info.

Definitely not worth the cost. Although flying does save time, I'm not sure how valuable this is. Our tour from take off to return was 6hrs, and became 9hrs as quoted on the website when you include the time to and from hotel.

Overall a nice experience but should be done much better to give customers more value for their money. They charge for the photo you take with the pilot at the beginning of the day, but after complaining about the delays/short trip, we were given our photos for free.

Don't get me wrong, the views are beautiful, but I would have preferred drive to the Canyon with a dedicated and engaging tour guide giving a lot of information.

Review Title: Put it on your bucket list!
Review Text:
If your one of those crazy, high adventure people, this may not be for you but if you're interested in a day you'll always remember, you should consider doing this one. There are several tours offered but I'm talking about the Scenic Canyon River Adventure.
The tour last 12 hours and starts EARLY! (ouch, but worth it). First you fly over the Grand Canyon (landing at Page AZ) then you board a 4 wheel drive vehicle (can be chilly - it's not enclosed) for a short drive to Antelope Canyon where you tour this amazingly beautiful rock formation (easy walk but has some tight places, be aware if you're bothered by tight spaces as I am). Then you board the same 4 wheel drive vehicle to be taken to where you will board a bus to be taken to the Glen Canyon dam area where you will get on a raft to raft down the Colorado. This is a smooth part of the river (no rapids) and is a peaceful, beautiful float. Here's where I think the tour is a little weak. The float lasted about 3 hours and I think it would have been just as good if they just went a little faster and turned it into 1 1/2 - 2 hours. Several of us felt this way even though we had a wonderful Navajo guide for the float. Kim was wonderful and this in no way reflects negatively on her, just saying they could pick up the pace without sacrificing any of the beauty of the float. The rafting trip ends at Lee's Ferry where you get on a bus that takes you back to the Tusayan area. It's a long day but when you consider the vantage points you achieve (above the Canyon, down in the Canyon (I don't want to ride a mule!), and floating down the Colorado) it's an amazing experience that you don't want to miss. We drove the Desertview portion of the South Rim the next day and felt like we were really able to see a lot of the Canyon in the two days we had there. There are plenty of stops for food (breakfast and lunch provided) and bathroom breaks. We booked online at the above link. It is rated the number 1 tour and we paid $788.00 for two (taxes, whatever all included). I also emailed this company before I booked with the questions I had and they responded quickly. Just do it!

Review Text:
We took the airplane tour to the Grand Canyon south rim from Las Vegas. While being picked up at the hotel at 4:30 am wasn't ideal, I was pleasantly surprised to find the shuttle driver was waiting for us exactly where we were told he would be and was even a few minutes early.

We were quickly transported to the airport terminal and checked in for our flight. About 15 min later, just enough time to grab a quick snack and browse the gift shop, our group was called and we boarded the plane.

The flight to the canyon lasted about an hour and there were headphones provided which would play music and called at different points of interest on our way. I really appreciated this since I've flown over the Grand Canyon several times and have never been able to tell exactly what I'm looking at.

On arriving we were quickly transferred to a shuttle bus that drove us to two different lookout points, giving us a little over an hour at each to explore, before taking us back to the terminal. The sights we stopped at were both beautiful. And the bus driver was very friendly and informative, offering to take group photos for us and providing lots of details about the canyon and its history.

The trip back to the hotel was just as efficient, arriving back at the hotel shortly before 1:00 pm. I don't think we were kept waiting for more than 10-15 min at any point during our trip.

I would definitely choose this tour company again. It may seem a little pricy at first, but it was well worth it to see the Grand Canyon and still getting to spend the rest of our day enjoying Vegas.

Review Text:
It's quite a few years ago since my wife and I did this flight but it was so memorable that it seems like only yesterday. After being picked up around teatime and taken to the airport everything was looking good and we boarded the small plane on time and off we went. A bit of a storm was brewing as we took off and the turbulence was quite bad, worsening as we passed Lake Mead and drew near to the Canyon. The views outside were spectacular and there was an informative commentary about the history and culture of the Canyon via the earphones provided.
Sadly, because of the turbulence, many of the passengers were making good and frequent use of sick-bags, instead of marvelling at the incredible views. However, the turbulence could hardly be blamed on the company and both pilots were very sympathetic and trying to be comforting (though for some this was in vain). The general feeling was that if the airplane had landed at or near the Canyon, then no-one would have re-boarded for the flight back to Vegas, so bad was the ride.
That apart, the trip was amazing and the memories, of the entire trip, are priceless and timeless.

Review Text: Four of us booked this tour expecting it to be the ultimate experience but we ended up feeling rushed but waiting around a lot. We were picked up at our hotel in a minibus, driven to another hotel to transfer to a coach and then driven 35/40 minutes to Boulder City to catch the flight. We waited around for approx 40 minutes to board the 30 minute flight to the canyon. The scenery was fantastic during the flight and the dam is amazing. When we landed we went to the terminal to again wait to be taken to the helicopter which took us on a short 5 minute flight to the canyon floor. We then went on a boat that travelled 5 minutes before stopping and the guide told us a bit of the history of the tribe that own that stretch of canyon and then took photos of us with our cameras. We then turned round and went back to board the helicopter for the 5 minute flight back to the terminal. We then boarded a bus to travel to the skywalk, where we queued for 15 minutes before being told it was closed and had been for a couple of hours due to lightning in the area. Back on the bus to the last stop for more photos and food, which we didn't have time to eat because we had been told to get back to the terminal to catch the flight back or we'd be stranded. We got back to the terminal and waited for 40 minutes to board the flight! Then, when we were back at the airport we waited 25 minutes for a bus to drive us to our hotel. Overall nothing can take away from the sheer scale and beauty of the canyon but I feel the tour that we booked tried to cram too much in (the tour is 7 hours long) so you were left feeling disappointed. I think it would be far better to do less and have more time to do it.

Review Text: We just completed our first Grand Canyon visit and the Scenic River Canyon Tour was the absolute best part of the trip. The entire tour could not have ran smoother. We arrived at the airport at 5:45 am, about 15 minutes from the El Tovar Lodge at Grand Canyon Village. Easy check in. We were provided a light breakfast with muffins, fruit, juice and coffee. We gathered in a comfortable lounge while waiting for the departure. We boarded about 6:20 with departure at 6:30. There were 6 passengers on our plane, every seat a window seat. Our pilot was delightful and informative. Although the plane was small, the flight was super smooth and thrilling. No matter how long you look, you can not see the depth and detail of the canyon from the rim like you can from the air. It is something I will never forget. After about a 50 minute flight, we landed in Page. We were soon met at the airport by a Navajo guide that would take us via 4-wheel vehicle to Antelope Canyon, a 20 min drive. The truck was open-air, so a little cool, but not too bad. At the canyon, the guide took us through, stopping and explaining exactly what we were seeing and the science and history around it. She gave us all tips on how to photograph the canyon and made this part of the tour a highlight. I promise you it will be the most beautiful place that you never heard of. After completing this part of the tour, we boarded a bus for a 10-12 min ride, and were provided a boxed lunch. The next stop was the canyon river portion of the tour. There we boarded a raft with our river guide 'Jenny'. You can sit in the provided cushion seating or the large pontoons. I recommend sitting in the seats just forward of Jenny's console. Those seats have back rests. Most folks ate their lunch as we headed down the river. Iced water and lemonade was provided. The 3 hour ride was incredible! It was slow and smooth, just fast enough to create a gentle, and appreciated breeze. You find yourself looking in all directions. The vistas in front and behind you. And the massive walls of rock on each side. In many places the 46 degree water was crystal clear and fish are easily seen. Jenny was a compete joy. She was funny, informative, courteous and helpful. She constantly informed us as to what we were seeing, and added great stories along the way. We made a stop along the way on a small sandy beach. Bath rooms are provided. You're also able to check out some  petroglyphs on the  canyon walls. After about a 30 min break, we re-boarded and continued down the river. More incredible views were along the way to Lees Ferry, where our motor coach back to the airport was waiting. There are bathrooms here as well. The bus was very comfortable and most folks napped on the way back. We stopped at Cameron Trading Post for about 30 min to stretch our legs and purchase souvenirs if you're inclined. The bus driver also was courteous and informative as we drove past more vistas along Desert View Drive. We returned to where we started,12 hours earlier. I can't think of any better way to experience the canyon. From the air, the Colorado River at the base and the rim during the drive back. I highly recommend the tour. It's a little pricey but you won't regret it.

Review Text:

Review Text: Excellently organised, from pick up, tour and drop off. Booked afternoon Delux tour 1055-2000! Pick up via bus to Bolder airport (30 mins), flight over Hoover Dam and west Rim (I think), then a bus to two spots on the south rim, Angel Bright and Matherson. For the flight book a window seat for one if you are traveling as a couple so you can sit together. I get air sick on small planes, I took some medication to assist with this and had no problem. As you are flying over the Canyons it can be a little bumpy however, well worth it when you see the amazing scenery. Seats 7A and 7C were the best for me right at the back plenty of leg room for my husband who is rather tall. Listen to the bus drivers for tips for the best photos. Review Title: Scenic Canyon River Adventure vs Imperial Ecostar Helicopter Tour in Grand Canyon South Rim
Review Text:
Both the tours left from Grand Canyon National Airport. Both I booked through Papillon, but Helicopter left from Papillon section of the airport whereas Scenic Canyon River Adventure left from the Grand Canyon Airlines section of the airport.
Helicopter tour - lasts 45min, $294 (I would give two stars)
Grand Canyon River Adventure - lasts 15-16hours, $394 (I would give five stars)

Imperial Ecostar (Two stars out of five)- The first day I took a helicopter ride and booked "Imperial Star Helicopter Ride" by Papillon. The helicopter is well maintained and a smooth ride. It was advertised as 40-50minutes, but my tour lasted 35minutes and we spend approximately 10-13minutes seeing the Grand Canyon. My pilot was not friendly as she preferred not to talk much and didn't seem to know answers to simple questions about the Grand Canyon. I am not sure whether the pilot was interested to be there. I was disappointed that I wasted nearly $289 with limited time over the Canyons, so decided to do a different one the next day and I got it right the second time - the Scenic Canyon River Adventure.

Scenic Canyon River Adventure (Five out of five stars) - I booked it through Papillon website, but the tour left from Grand Canyon Airlines from Grand Canyon National Airport. I couldn't get enough of this tour as I enjoyed throughly every minute of it. It costed $394 for the whole day, breakfast and lunch included, it lasted 15 hours, we left at 6am. When we arrived at 6am in GC airport, our breakfast box was waiting. We boarded on a small plane to fly over the Grand Canyon to Page Airport for an hour, our plane was an eight seater plane with brilliant views for everyone as all seats were window seats. We flew over Grand Canyon, saw Glen Canyon Dam and had beautiful views. In fact I enjoyed my views from this plane than the helicopter tour I did the previous day. We had a short break in Page airport where we could use toilets and was given a brief briefing on what the next tour would be - Antelope Canyon visit. We sat on back of trucks which were converted to be tour trucks with two rows of seats backing each other thereby all of us got good views of the town on the way to the Upper Antelope Canyon. It was an interesting unique rocky fun experience in this truck to the Antelope Canyon, I wouldn't want to trade it any other way. We spent some time visiting the Upper Antelope Canyon where our tour guide showed all the interesting views of Upper Antelope Canyon. I wish this tour had included the Lower Antelope Canyon also. We were then taken to Colorado River Discovery Office where we had 45 minutes to relax in the cafe and take a toilet break. We could fill up our water bottles in the cafe. Big buses came to pick us up to the Glen Canyon Dam site. We were given packed lunches when we boarded the bus.The long tunnel ride by bus was one of the most unique drives I have encountered - I would suggest to sit on the front seats as it has better view in the tunnel than the rear ones if you are interested in watching the dark tunnel drive. The tunnel was a two mile long dark tunnel dug through the canyon walls with small window of light dug out for ventilation. On the end of the tunnel was the base of Glen Canyon Dam and our motorized raft with our tour guide. Our guide Brian was knowledgable, interesting, interactive, fun and made our 4 1/2 hours ride as perfect as it could be! We had two toilet breaks, two brief swimming breaks, stopped at petroglyps, took several pictures, it was serene and beautiful in the Colorado river. Interestingly, I couldn't picture the feel of Horseshoe bend while in the river as well as we could see it, since our view was limited by the Canyon walls. (So went the following day driving to see it from top of the Canyon). We had plenty of drinking water on board also. Our motorized raft ended in Historic Lees Ferry Port where buses were waiting to pick us up to drive back to Grand Canyon National Airport, it was a long drive for 3 1/2 hrs. We stopped at Cameron Trading Post where there were interesting Navajo Indian Reservation handicrafts, gifts, cafe, toilets and hotel. Our bus driver pointed out to the interesting tourist spots on the way back and stopped to drop some people off at the South Rim before getting back to Grand Canyon National Airport.

Review Title: Excursión muy completa aunque un poco larga

Sobrevuelas el cañón mas o menos una hora y luego te llevan a Antilope Canyon (nuestro guía, buenísimo). Posteriomente, desciendes el rio unas dos horas, con un par de paradas para que los niños y los valientes puedan bañarse (el agua está bastante fria). Picnic para desayunar y comer (mas que aceptable). Para mi, el tramo del rio, demasiado largo y un poco tedioso, bajo un sol de justicia. No ayuda que mi inglés sea nefasto, porque el guía era excelente. Al final, vuelta al aeropuerto en autocar (más de tres horas). Muy bien organizado y profesionales excelentes (el conductor del autocar estvo explicando cosas interesantes del Grand Canyon durante las dos últimas horas del viaje. Se estropeó el aire acondicionado del autocar y nos trajeron otro. Cuesta un dinerito (unos 375 dólares) pero vale la pena porque ves el Canyon desde el aire y desde el agua. Eso sí, acabas reventado. No se os olvide sombrero y crema solar !! En la barca y en el autocar, dan agua gratis. La excursión dura aproximadamente 12,5 horas. Te dan la opción de pagar 10 dólares más por tener ventana grande en la avioneta. No vale la pena. Se ve igual en todos los sitios. (A no ser que vayas solo y te toque pasillo).

Review Title: Grand Canyon was amazing, getting there not so much
Review Text:
We did the connoisseur trip to the South Rim. Our bus arrived exactly on time to take us to the airport. The driver did seem like he was in a hurry & was short with some of the passengers but they were late so I guess that is to be expected. We arrived at the airport & didn't have a long wait to check in. Once checked in we had approx 30mins before our flight left which was enough time to get some food & water at the cafe in the airport.
Our pilot was nice & friendly. The plane was very cramped which I guess is to be expected but if you are taller than 6 foot you will find it very cramped. Also the day was very hot & the plane doesn't have aircon. It was also a very turbulent flight which made my wife & I feel quite ill. The upside to all this is the views from the aircraft are amazing from the Hover Damn through to different parts of the Canyon. There is an audio tour of everything you are seeing which is great, however the music that goes with it is terrible.
We arrived safely & then were directed to a bus to travel to the canyon. The bus driver again was quite short with the other passengers who didn't speak a ton of english so I don't think they understand what was required anyway. The driver was nice to us but I believe there should have been more direction on where to go once we arrived at the airport & how much time before we left on the bus, so people knew whether to rush to the toilet or not. Once arriving at the canyon it was everything & more than we expected. Our travel back on the bus was fine however the plane ride back (which is about 1hr) was very turbulent, after the rough flight we were made to wait on the tarmac for a couple of mins in the heat for no apparent reason which added to the sickness. The bus ride back to our hotel was quick & we didn't need to wait long.
If I had to do it again, a helicopter ride would be my pick.

Review Text:
We did the Tour Adventure (this company provides a wide variety of Grand Canyon tours-- you have a lot of options depending on how much time and money you want to spend. However, I do think this particular tour option gives you the most "bang for the buck".) which included a plane ride over the Grand Canyon, a visit to Antelope Canyon, and a rafting trip down the Colorado through Glen Canyon. It takes the whole day (we had to be at the airport near the South Rim by 6 am and were returned there at about 6:00 pm) and is well worth it-- you get a great sense of the whole area. You see the Grand Canyon from above (which is a vaster, more expansive view than you get hiking in it-- a different way to see it than we had the day before), see the canyon walls from below as you raft down the river (though, this is through Glen Canyon, not the Grand Canyon-- rafting waters through the Glen Canyon are really calm while the waters through the Grand Canyon are rougher. This is the relaxed, scenic way to raft the river.) and the breathtaking interior of Upper Antelope Canyon which is open only by reserved tour (you can't just walk in yourself-- you have to have a guide).
Everyone on this tour, from the pilot to the river guide to the bus driver who took us to our car at the end of the day, was enthusiastic and friendly. It was well run and well organized (and, even had well-timed bathroom breaks to accommodate the long day and the fact that, if it's hot, you'll want to drink a lot of water). The food provided was good-- overall, this is a nicely comprehensive day and a great trio of ways to experience the Grand Canyon and around.

Review Title: dramatic canyon, great way to see lots of it although a little rushed
Review Text:
First i will cover the canyon, which is amazing and dramatic it is like nothing I have seen before with vivid colours, sheer drops, and scale. It is a true stunning natural wonder.

The second thing i will cover is our 'tour' which more accurately would be described as a multiple experience bookings bundled together. The way this provider achieves so much at its price is by not really offering a true personal tour. e.g. our package was for airport transfer, a small public flight from bolder to canyon airport (via hover dam), helicopter transfer down, brief boat ride, helicopter transfer up, public shuttle bus to lookup, meal ticket, public shuttle bus back, public flight back to bolder, airport transfer. As state it is great value but you are effectively on a semi public service so are waiting around for departure times, rather than being on a private tour.

The boat ride was a little disappointing, it was quite brief, didn't go particularly far, and simply went up the river and back down the river. While it was a novelty i would have preferred being able to actually walk around a little which you are not allowed to do with strict paths between the helipad and the boat pontoon being marked.

The food provided was more than enough and quite tasty, we ate at guano point with brilliant views out over the canyon.

Review Title: Grand Canyon was Great, Scenic Airlines not so much...
Review Text:
The Scenic Airlines Grand Canyon Connoisseur Tour is a great way to see the south rim of the Grand Canyon if you are visiting from Las Vegas. A bus tour is the least expensive but makes for a very long day. Of the 14 hours slated for a bus tour, 10 hours of it is spent driving back and forth. Only about 3 hours of the time is spent actually viewing the canyon. Driving it yourself is also tedious unless you plan on staying overnight. The helicopter tours also look great, but are almost twice the price. So the Grand Canyon Connoisseur airplane tour was a good option. One hour of flying there, then transfer by bus to tour the canyon for 3 hours, and then a one hour ride back. They will also pick you up and drop you off from your Las Vegas hotel.

However you decide to see the canyon, scour the internet for the best price and tour to suit your needs. There’s a ton of choices and different prices for the same types of tours, so shop around.

Scenic, Papillion and Grand Canyon Airlines are all the same company, departing from the Boulder City airport, located about 45 minutes from the strip. We found the best price for the tour with Scenic. Grand Canyon Airlines has the exact same tour, but was slightly more. There was also a difference in price, depending on what time of day you book your tour. Our 9:15AM tour was the most expensive, the 12:30PM was less, and the 6:15AM was the least expensive.

Here are a few tips: When you book, give an accurate weight and even overestimate your weight a little. They weigh you before you get on the plane, and that includes your purse, camera, water bottle, etc., so keep that in mind. If you get motion sickness, take dramamine or bonine beforehand. The plane is small (about 19 passengers), and it got quite bumpy for a good portion of the flight. Do not pay extra for a window seat. Our plane had two seats on each side and the windows are very large. If you are a couple they generally seat you together, so one of you should get a window seat.

Now the GOOD:
Beautiful aerial view of the Hoover Dam, Lake Mead, the Colorado River and the Grand Canyon.
Bus tour took you to Bright Angel and Mather Point. This is the most impressive and the widest and deepest part of the canyon. Plenty of time to souvenir shop too.
Gigi, our bus driver was fabulous! She was a lot of fun and gave a lot of interesting information. They also had another guide to speak Japanese for part of our group.

And the BAD:
Our tour was scheduled to leave at 9:15am. The Boulder Terminal was very hectic, and had several groups all leaving around the same time for different plane and helicopter tours. They “color coded” each group to make things simple. Each of the groups were called, except for our “purple” group. We were left sitting there well past the 9:15 departure time. We went up and asked after it was a half hour late and was told they were waiting for the pilot. 20 more minutes went by and someone else asked the desk and was not given any more information. When the pilot finally showed up he told our group that the audio portion of the tour wasn’t working and they were trying to fix it. We finally started toward the gate a full HOUR past our original departure time. No one told us we would be delayed, and were still not sure what the real problem was. They just let us sit there and didn’t say a word. We’ve been on several tours including helicopter tours so we know the general routine. In our opinion, it was very unprofessional of Scenic not to inform us of a major delay. When the pilot finally showed up he acted like nothing happened. Everyone was fuming.

We ended up having a great tour in spite of the bad start, but we really feel Scenic should review this incident and handle it more professionally in the future.

Review Title: Lovely views and good day. Only wish it was longer!
Review Text:
Toying between the coach tour and an air tour of some kind, we went on the Grand Canyon Connoisseur tour and I would recommend this tour above the coach tour any day. It takes a lot less time to get there and if you take the early tours you still have time in the day to do other stuff around Las Vegas.

You do have to be ready 2 hours before your scheduled flight as they do a round up from all the hotels then put you on a bus to get to boulder city for the flight. If you are on the first am flight this can be very early! The tour takes you via a small propeller plane to the south rim and you get amazing views on the flight as you fly over the hoover dam, Lake mead and parts of the grand canyon itself. You also get to see the west rim including the skywalk.

Once there you board a coach that takes you to the park which is about 15 mins. You stop at 2 spots which allows you about an hour free time each at of the 2 spots, them being bright angel lodge and mather point. You get provided a lunch but no choice for vegetarian options. It would be good if you put a request out as part of the booking process for dietary requirements. The driver is knowledgeable with a good sense of humour and provides some good info and places to take good photos from.

Just wish there was more time and maybe another stop added to further enhance the experience. Yes it is more expensive than the coach tour but cheaper than a helicopter tour and you get good views and time at the park with half a day still remaining to do other stuff. All massive bonuses above the coach tour.

Review Text: We booked the Highlights Tour online, which offered 2 tours at discounted rates (saving 80 dollars per ticket - a saving for us of 320 dollars). The 9.00am tour meant a pick-up time of 6.30 at our hotel in Las Vegas, so we opted for the 3.00pm tour which had a pick-up time of 1.30. The 30-minute minibus ride out to the airfield in Boulder City was fast and comfortable. We were checked in immediately, and waited for about 45 minutes in the terminal building for our group to be called. The problem with booking the 3.00pm tour (the last tour of the day) is that if for any reason the plane gets delayed on its previous tour, there isn't much room for maneuver as daylight starts fading fast after 4.00pm. We were told at 3.00pm that the flight would be delayed by one hour and were offered an immediate full refund and return bus to Las Vegas or the option to rebook the tour. As it was the last day of our visit, we decided to chance it anyway as were told that we would see everything except the return 30 minutes of the tour. Unfortunately, the plane landed at 3.50pm, the obligatory photo with each passenger/couple/family still had to be taken with the pilot before boarding, and we then waited at the end of the runway for the returning planes to land before we could take off. We took off at 4.20 and the light was fading fast. It is a 70-minute round-trip, we actually got about 15 minutes of seeing the canyon before it was too dark to see anything. My advice would be don't book the 3.00pm Scenic Highlights Tour unless you have the possibility to rebook on another day - set the alarms and go for the 9.00 tour instead.

Review Title: Not the best use of time
Review Text: We had a great time at the Canyon, but only wish, that out of a 9-hour tour, we could have had more than 1.5 hours at the Canyon itself. We were told to be ready at 4:40 for our hotel pick-up, and finally arrived at the air terminal around an hour later, after numerous hotel stops and one shuttle bus change. If we had driven our own rental car, we could have shaved about 35 minutes off that portion and gained another half-hour of much-needed sleep, LOL! The flight was beautiful, and we both got window seats. Note: the views and light in the morning are much nicer on the left side of the aircraft. Once at Grand Canyon airport, we were efficiently shuttled into a huge bus (very roomy, but about 3x bigger than our group of 15 actually needed). The driver was friendly and personable, and even went back to pick up stragglers from our first stop after delivering us to the second one. But, at 45 minutes for each of 2 stops, it was nowhere near enough time at the park. If we had flown back right away after driving back to the airport it would have been one thing, but we were made to wait about an hour and a half before our flight back -- which is time I would rather have spent at the park itself. To top it all off, we found it was the same tour we could have booked through Scenic for about a hundred dollars less; the only reason we booked through this company instead is that they actually explained the plane configuration and guaranteed one of us would get a window seat (Scenic told us it would be totally random whether we would get one or not).

Review Title: "So it's a little pricey ... but hey, you only live once!"
Review Text:
This was the activity that I chose for mine and my husband's recent trip to Arizona - the 12 1/2 hour Scenic Canyon River Adventure that covered air, land and water. And if I don't say so myself, I chose well.

Our excursion began at 6 am at the Grand Canyon Airport - less than a mile from The Grand Hotel where we were staying. At check-in we were weighed (this included anything we were carrying) and given a boxed breakfast (OJ, small yogurt, banana muffins, cheese stick and a granola bar). Color-coded wrist bands (green for our group) were affixed to our arm. At promptly 6:30 am approxiately 20 persons boarded the small aircraft with each one having their own window seat (we didn't have to pay extra for it). Take off was smooth (and uneventful) and after ten minutes or so the Canyon appeared in all of its splendor as the sun rose casting a myriad of colors - soft pinks, deep reds and warm golds wherever its rays touched ... simply breathtaking! There were headphones on the plane that provided info on the scenes unfolding below as the plane soared onward. A half hour into our flight the clear blue waters of Lake Powell emerged. All too soon we touched down (smoothly) on the other side of the Canyon in Page, AZ.

After a fifteen minute wait at the small airport, our group was shuttled onto retro-fitted pick-up trucks for an often bumpy ride to Antelope Canyon where other tour groups were already gathered. I tend to be a bit claustrophobic so thankfully it wasn't very dark inside the narrow passageways. Light spilled from above creating some spectacular photo-op's. Upon reaching the end of the long tunnel we then turned around and retraced our steps back to where we started. Loaded back onto the pick-up's, we were then driven to the Colorado River Discovery building in Page, AZ.

It was another 30 or 45 minutes before several large coach buses pulled in front of the building. Dozens of people were assembled and wore a variety of colored coded wrist-bands. Each person was handed a boxed lunch (turkey sandwich, chips, chocolate chip cookies and an apple) as they boarded the buses. We were driven through a dark, 2-mile inclined tunnel that brought us down to the river basin at Glen Canyon Dam. Given hard-hats to wear as we were told it was mandatory due to its being a government run facility, we walked a short distance over to the large rafts. Each raft easily accommodated 18 - 20 people. My husband and I were fortunate to have been on the vessel led by Brett, an informative and often amusing guide who regaled us with many stories and folklore of the Colorado River. He also played a mean recorder! For fifteen miles we floated ever so slowly down the majestic river surrounded by massive stone walls that stretched upwards hundreds of feet. Twice Brett made two short stops where a few brave (or crazy) souls jumped into frigid 47 degree water and we trekked a short distance to spot ancient petroglyphs drawn on rock walls. Upon docking we were resorted according to wrist band colors and directed to the appropriate coach bus. Most, including myself, fell asleep during the two hour return trip back to the Grand Canyon Airport.

To say that the entire excursion - plane, land and float was spectacular and incredibly humbling is an understatement. I highly recommend it! If you have the opportunity to take this tour, DO IT! It was money well spent for the experience of a life-time!

TIP: Wear a hat and bring and use plenty of sunscreen. The tour company provides water.

We were picked up right on time, the little plane was great (big windows, you can see in the cockpit a little) and our pilots were very personable. My friend and I got lucky and had a jeep all to ourselves. Our guide was fantastic, and a jeep lets you go to lookout spots that buses aren't allowed to stop at. Review Title: DO NOT DO THIS TOUR, SCENIC AIRLINES ARE LIERS
Review Text:
I know this is a lot BUT PLEASE READ BEFORE BOOKING THIS TOUR!
I booked this tour for two people at a cost of $646.00 bucks the Thursday before the trip. I spent over an hour on the phone getting all the details about this 1 hour trip. At no point did the booking Agent tell me there was a $100.00 up charge for any person weighing over 300lbs while holding all the gear (i.e. cloths, water, camera, food, bag) they are taking on the plane. I received my Reservation Confirmation by email shortly after I booked, great no problem. The next day without as much as a phone call I got a new reservation by email with a $100.00 “Comfort Seat” charge. So I called the number on the new reservation, and asked what a “Comfort Seat” charge was. The girl (Aliett Chavez) I spoke with said it was because I entered a weight of 310lbs when I first booked it. I then when on to say if I have to pay an extra $100 dollars for my weight I want to cancel the trip. She then asked me to hold came back and said she would waive the fee. She then stated “I don’t know why they put that on there”, and she said she was sending me a new reservation with that charge (which she did) removed. Upon arrival at 5:45am, 45 minutes before the flight leaves they put you on a scale in front of everyone and let you know you’re over 300lbs and you have to pay the “COMFORT SEAT“ charge, SO HUMILIATING. Let me clear the air now for anyone wondering, THERE’S NO SUCH THING AS A “COMFORT SEAT” on this plane. This is their PC way of charging more money for overweight people. They claim it’s a “Weight distribution issue” but I can assure you that’s not the reason in this case. Our tour had 3 empty seats which were on the opposite side of the plane that I was sitting on; if it’s a “Weight distribution issue” wouldn’t the empty seats be on MY side???? I would say the tour was not fully booked, and I couldn’t cancel because it was within 24 hour departure time, and there’s NO REFUNDS, and they know that.
Upon arrival the Captain explains the tour is going to be an hour. He then goes on to say because of some agreement with the Grand Canyon National Park we can’t fly directly to the GC. Even though the airport is ONLY 8 miles directly south of the rim. He says we have to travel for less than 10 minutes due east before dropping into the canyon. Now I timed the due east time and it was almost 20 minutes before we reached the rim. We went about 20 miles east then the 8 miles north to get to the south rim. Once over the GC we only spend about 15 minutes on our way to Glenn Canyon and Lake Powell which is where we spent most of the flight time before landing in Page AZ. The main reason I would not recommend doing this trip is because its focus is Glenn Canyon and Lake Powell, NOT the Grand Canyon. It’s almost like they are flying through the GC as a short cut to get to Glenn Canyon & Page AZ. Let me just say Glenn Canyon is EXTREMELY BORING compared to the Grand Canyon, almost to the point of a letdown. You would be much better off paying a little more for the helicopter rides which focus ONLY on the Grand Canyon, which I would have done on the spot the morning of but as you know I would have lost my full fare. Please do yourself a favor and save you money on the Scenic Airlines Company. I hope this helps???

Review Text:
The views are superb, and the ride was relatively smooth. The landing upon return was so easy I didn't even know we were back on the ground.

Those are pluses, but there was one huge minus which so negatively impacted the trip for my daughter and me as to threaten to ruin it, as it did for sure for the young woman in the seat ahead of me, and probably others as well.

This big minus would be as follows: despite the following description on the Grand Canyon Airlines web page, "The passenger cabin is climate controlled with heat and air conditioning to allow for the most comfortable ride," the cabin of our plane was NOT air conditioned, on a one hundred degree day in late August.

In fact, the cabin started out very, very warm, continued to grow warmer still, and by the time our tour was up, it was unbearably stuffy and hot.

This made for one heck of an uncomfortable three quarters of an hour, with the view below taking second fiddle to faintness from the heat. Any suggestion of airsickness was amplified by the oppressive atmosphere of the plane's cabin. A cool flow of air would have made all the difference in the world.

As we walked from the plane to the building I asked one of the pilots why there had been no air conditioning. He immediately said, "Because it wasn’t working."

He then quickly collected himself and said, "We do run the air conditioning, but it can only reduce the temperature a certain amount." Ah yes, I think, from his lips, the truth came first, and caution followed.

I told him that in my opinion it was not flying that had made people sick on his plane, but the heat. Airsickness bags may be a necessary convenience, but how much better not to have to use them, especially on a flight that is so expensive and has been so eagerly anticipated by the sufferers, who now find themselves too ill to enjoy it.

I would have loved to be able to say this was a wonderful experience, but the heat and stuffiness in the cabin was literally sickening. Any discomfort from the motion of the plane would easily have been counterbalanced by a flow of fresh, cool air, of which there was none.

I was very disappointed to have my daughter's and my experience--as well as that of the others on our plane--negatively impacted by an equipment malfunction which was never acknowledged, for which we received no apology, and certainly no suggestion of a voucher or even a partial refund.

Review Text:
Fizemos um passeio de avião saindo do aeroporto em Tusayan e sobrevoamos o Grand Canyon. Foi maravilhoso. Chegamos em Page e dali seguimos por terra para Antelope Canyon. Por fim, embarcamos em um bote flutuador (com motor) e seguimos pelo Rio Colorado até "Lee's Ferry", de onde voltamos de ônibus até o aeroporto.
Os pontos negativos são:
1- O passeio pelo rio é bonito mas longo demais.
2- Na volta, o ônibus para em um restaurante em Cameron. A guia estava muito apressada e mal deu tempo de ir ao banheiro e comer alguma coisa.
O restante foi muito bom. Uma experiência maravilhosa.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: Trato excelente y buena organización. Merece la pena a pesar de que no es barato. El avión está muy bien preparado y los 40 minutos que dura el vuelo son muy entretenidos.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: Fiz o trajeto até o south rim no grand canyon ! altamente recomendado ! dura 1 dia inteiro, e vale totalmente a pena, cada centavo, vistas espetaculares, o voo no avião é bem seguro, conta com sistema de som individual. O passeio de helicoptero sobre o grand canyon foi épico !
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Non siamo neanche partiti. Nessun piano B
Review Text:
Puntata a Las Vegas esclusivamente per questo trip aereo prenotato (e pagato) con tre mesi di anticipo. Sveglia alle 6.00. Alle 6.30 passa all'Hotel un pulmino che carica solo i prenotati per elicottero. Dopo 10 minuti ritorna dicendo che si era sbagliato e ci carica (prima indicazione di dilettantismo). Vengono annunciati 20 minuti di marcia. In realtà diventano un'ora. Al terminal regna il caos (seconda indicazione di dilettantismo). Ci danno un adesivo colorato da apporre sul petto. La mia famiglia viene raggruppata con alcuni turisti orientali. Partono tutti i gruppi. Rimaniamo desolatamente soli e ci viene annunciato che l'aereo ha dei problemi tecnici. Nessun aereo di riserva. Nessuna alternativa se non un tour limitato in elicottero, ma nel pomeriggio. Nessuna possibilità per il giorno successivo. Richiedo il rimborso, che verrà effettuato entro tre giorni a mezzo bonifico. Offrono ad ogni membro un buono per un drink al bar del terminal. La sensazione è di una compagnia non molto professionale. Se questa è l'organizzazione, caratterizzata dalla mancanza di piani alternativi (a fronte di una clientela internazionale), è naturale chiedersi come possa essere l'efficienza di autovelivoli e piloti.
Da notare che questi signori esigono dalla clientela la massima precisione, come ad esempio chiamare telefonicamente (non basta una mail) il giorno prima per confermare, pena la cancellazione del volo. E poi ti pesano per vedere se superi la soglia per un supplemento di costo...
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: La meilleure façon de voir la grandeur du grand canyon
Review Text:
Nous avons fait le tour de 45min depuis le South Rim, dans un avion qui peut accueillir jusqu'à 18 personnes: 6 rangées de 3 donc on peut se trouver au milieu mais on voit quand même tout très bien. On est placé en fonction de son poids sur un des 3 sièges.
Nous en gardons des magnifiques photos comme souvenir.
Et pourtant nous avons eu partiellement de la pluie et le ciel était en grand parti couvert de nuages. Le vol à failli être annulé pour risque d'orages.
Nous avions le vol de 14h et a 11h le ciel était tout bleu. Cela montre avec quelle rapidité le temps peut changer ici!
La prestation vaut largement son prix et on vient ici une fois dans sa vie, donc il faut en profiter.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Wow- what a nice way to see the Grand Canyon
Review Text: The planes are great with huge windows. With 3 in a row, everybody gets to see everything. The whole process of buying the tickets, "check in", boarding is super fast and efficient, you will not loose a lot of time and the flights are on time. The pilots are nice and fun. But most of all, 40 minutes of flying above the Canyon is absutely fabulous and unforgettable, We wanted to the get the helicopter tour but it was sold out. I guess however that the regular airplanes are at least as good - and a little cheaper.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
Im Rahmen einer grösseren Tour flogen wir zum Sonnenaufgang vom Grand Canyon Airport nach Page. Dieser Flug dauert rund eine Stunde.

Die Grand Canyon Airlines setzt spezielle 2-motorige Hochdecker namens "Vistaliner" der Firma De Havilland ein. Der Name kommt daher, dass das Flugzeug nur Fensterplätze mit ausgezeichneter Sicht an grossen Fenstern bietet - und auch nur 17.

Der Flug entlang des Canyons wird von Kommentaren auf Band (via Kopfhörer in der gewünschten Sprache) begleitet. Diese sind ausgezeichnet redigiert und technisch perfekt (auch in perfektem Deutsch) aufgenommen.

Ein Erlebnis!

Noch ein kleiner Hinweis: Jeder Passagier wird vor dem Boarding und dem Ausstellen der Boarding Card mit Platz am Check-In-Schalter automatisch gewogen, damit später das Flugzeug schön austariert ist.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: From the flight over The Grand Canyon,  to the jeep trip to Antelope Canyon, to the raft trip down Glen Canyon,  the whole experience was amazing. Our guides were friendly and well informed and the day ran really smoothly. Highly recommended.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Soaring at a Gentle Pace Over the Canyon
Review Text:
We took the air tour on the STOL (short take off and landing) aircraft and were not disappointed. We did the Grand Discovery Air Tour, a 45 minute narrated run about the Canyon that was just right. We saw immense parts of the Canyon, including the North Rim, from such a wonderful vantage point and without the crowds that swarm over the South Rim. It was a real treat!

Note on seating: the rows are two-by-two on the right side of the plane, but single seats on the left. We did not have advance reservations so we had what was available, which meant my boyfriend and I did not get to sit together. I was not happy about this as the agent did not inform us of the seating arrangements when we purchased the tickets. We naturally assumed the seats were together. The company needs to stress to agents that they be clear about the seating so passengers know what to expect. Hence I was frowning when they took the official photo of us just before boarding! It worked out o.k., since we were behind each other and we both had window seats this way, but we should have been informed of the seating and choices on other flights.

All in all, a great ride. The plane only goes 100 mph, and it's altitude is low for sight-seeing, so you really get a great view and great ride. The Colorado River is up pretty close that way, you can even see the rapids!

A great way to see the Canyon. Thumbs up!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Bus Tour from Las Vargas ,national Park parking
Review Text: The Buses are available of A.c. coat he's of two By to to Take you to round tour from to.These buses halts at all visitor points to take you to nearest attraction of cannon beauty and attractions.You will get rest room and other needs like foods at subside rates.We took water and other beverages for summer heat.The tour was so attractive that other missed places of great nature thrust of visiting has been in mind.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: If you want to see the Grand Canyon from every possible angle, you must take this tour. Is worth every penny, plus guides are excellent. From the plane to the antelope to the raft, it was incredible. Our raft guide Brent was excellent. Full of energy, lots of info, funny, the guy knew his stuff. Thanks for this amazing experience.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: I gave this 3 stars because if it weren't for my crying 1.5 year old, my screaming 3 year old and my vomiting 7 year old, it would have been great.  Oddly my 5 year old was cool as a cucumber.  We visited the weekend before the 4th of July and there were high wind advisories for the weekend.  I should have known better but my husband really wanted to go.  There was a lot of turbulence.  But if you can get over the turbulence the views were amazing!  The pilot did tell us, after we safely landed, that in the morning there is less wind.  We rode on the Vistaliner.  It had two seats on one side and and one seat on the other.  They offer headphones that are noise canceling and have a narration.  Windows were very large to take in the beautiful view.  You take your photo with the pilot before take off which is available for purchase after the flight for $20.  If we go again we are going to take the first flight in the morning!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
We were a party of 3 and did the 45 mins plane flight from the South Rim. The plane was smaller than advertised as we had been told it was 3 seats across, (two plus one) however the plane we flew on had only one seat at each side so everyone had a window. The upside - everyone had a window, the downside, the windows were not as large as those shown on the website pictures.

In all though it was a great experience and I would consider this a must do if you are in the area. Great views, nothing like you will see from the rim. There were headphones and narration to highlight areas on interest.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
Grand Canyon Airlines do a great job of a 40 minute flight over the Canyon. Booking is easy online, can pay with creditcard, make a phonecall to reconfirm your flight, and Bingo! We booked on the same day we flew.

Pretty bumpy ride, did not bother us, easy opportunity to take glorious pictures, just switch off your flash and put focus on manual to infinite. Advantage over helicopter flight is that this takes longer and everybody has a window seat - and it is cheaper!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: Three of us signed up for the plane ride about a month in advance. There were really high winds that day (40 mph+), but the company didn't cancel so we went for the ride. 15 minutes in, another passenger started vomiting. Somehow the three of us survived the turbulence, which took all of the fun out of the amazing views and great narrations. About 30 minutes in we were wishing it was over- the turbulence was intolerable and quite frightening, and making us so sick we were doing all we could not to vomit. After getting off the plane we were so nauseated that we had to lay down at the airport for about an hour before getting back in the car. Go on a calm day- not worth the cost to be sick in a tiny plane in high winds.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
We made reservations for our airplane flight less than 2 weeks out via the website. We remembered to call more than 24 hours in advance to confirm our flight. Our flight departed on time and we had incredible views of the canyon. Our pilot was very friendly and rather humorous. Our plane was small and seated 8, so everyone had a window seat in order to observe the Grand Canyon. I would use this airline again and would recommend them to others.

We had one little hiccup, which the company took care of without too much trouble. According to the reservation paperwork, guests can pay $10 extra for a guaranteed window seat. When we called to confirm our reservation we asked to guarantee the window seats. They said they could only take a "request" at that time and made note in their system. When we checked in for the flight, I inquired into our request. I was told that our plane was an 8 seater and a all seats were window seats, which was great. But then they requested that we pay the additional $10 per person because we had requested the seats... even though EVERYONE would have a window seat. Again, they did remove the "request" from our reservation and all was good, but it was a little frustrating for a minute. Thankfully they did the right thing.

One thing to note - the men's bathroom was under construction when we visited (June 9, 2013) and all male guests had to use the port-a-potties outside. I was very thankful that the women's bathroom was fully functional!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: A highlight of our Grand Canyon visit
Review Text:
OK so I'm a bit biased because I like light aircraft flights, much better than soulless airliners. An aerial view of the Grand Canyon is a must see, we got some great photos as well as just sitting back enjoying the view and I suspect you would not see any more from a pricier helicopter flight.

As to the organisation, efficient, amiable, no delays; the aircraft was full but there was plenty of room (and I'm tall) with no restrictions on the views.

The Grand Canyon lives up to the hype and this flight enhanced the experience.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Une vue imprenable sur le Grand Canyon
Review Text: Même si désormais les avions offrent 3 places de front, la vue par les larges hublots est parfaite. Les commentaires associées complètent les superbes vues car les vols ne sont effectués que dans de bonnes conditions météo. L'aérodrome est de plus tout à côté du Grand Canyon National Park. De plus le prix demeure abordable !
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: Wow, what an amazing trip! Nothing compares to that experience, really. We just took the 45 min tour from the South Rim airport. Checking in went smooth and the staff was friendly. The ride itself was just incredible. Those views are remarkable. If you're visiting the Grand Canyon, please don't skip this attraction.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: The best way to see the Grand Canyon
Review Text: This is a review of the Scenic Airlines - Grand Canyon National Park. We took the 45 minute flight in an aeroplane, which is the same cost as a 20 minute flight in a helicopter. The flight takes you all of the way around the Grand Canyon. We were lucky to chose a perfect day in terms of weather, calm, sunny and blue sky. The flight is great, it gives you a really good perspective of the Grand Canyon. its comfortable, relatively quiet the plane takes approx 18 -21 passengers. Excellent views from all seats, there are 3 in each row, two by window either side and one in the middle, all get great views. If you're going all the way to the Grand Canyon, these operate from the South rim airport, don't miss this opportunity as well as walking in and around the Canyon. This beats all the views you get walking and helps give you an idea of the scale of the place. Its awesome and breathtaking. Thanks for a great flight, it was the highlight of our two day visit to the Grand Canyon. Remember to book online beforehand for the best price.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: I took the Indian Country With Skywalk tour on March 20th.  They were waiting outside of my Las Vegas hotel right on time.  After a pleasant ride to Boulder City Airport, we waited a short while before boarding a clean and comfortable 19-passenger DeHavilland DHC-6-300 plane. The plane ride was very nice to the Grand Canyon West airport, passing over the dam along the way.  From there we were able to take the hop-on-hop-off buses to the two stops included with tour.  Both places offered wonderful views of the canyon, with the Skywalk at one and a tasty lunch at the other. Lots of fantastic photo opportunities along the edge of a 4000-foot drop!  The pilots and ground crew were all very pleasant. I would gladly do it again.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
Hermoso paseo para conocer la inmensidad del cañón, se aprecia una vista totalmente diferente que desde la pasarela.
Todo funciono perfecto, desde la reserva online, envió de voucher y salida en horario. El tour tiene audio en distintos idiomas que comentan datos del cañón.
Muy recomendable!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: Une des façons les plus émouvantes de parcourir des yeux la magnificence du lieu , avec comme point d'orgue le point de partage des eaux entre le " Petit Colorado " à la livrée turquoise , et le fleuve roi aux nuances émeraude ...
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Grand Canyon national park airplane/ground tour
Review Text: Fabulous day! The staff were outstanding from pick up to drop off, they were a delightful team who's enthusiasm was infectious.  The South rim of the Canyon is a little further to fly but the views are breathtaking.  2 hours are spent on the ground split into 2 park viewing  areas.  This trip wets the thirst for return holidays! The views from the air (1 hour each way) are spectacular!!!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
Nous avons fait le highlight tour en avion il y a quelques jours et nous en reparlons chaque jour des étoiles plein les yeux.

Nous avons été enchantés de notre trip : d'abord un petit shuttle est venu nous chercher à notre hotel pour nous emmener à l'aéroport de Boulder City.
Nous étions une petite dizaine a bord.

Arrivés sur place, pas de cohue : 4 guichets ouverts où l'on vous pese (très discrètement), vérifie vos passeports et vous attribue une couleur.
Nous avons attendu 20 min entre l'enregistrement et le moment où nous avons embarqué.

Devant l'avion, le pilote vous explique les consignes de sécurité et vous attribue un siège.
Il y a 10 places, le pilote compris, et chacun a sa fenêtre.
Un casque est à votre disposition avec des explications, dans différents langues, dont en français.

Lors du décollage, ca secoue pas mal ; mais une fois dans les airs, le paysage vous coupe tellement le souffle que vous ne prêtez plus attention aux secousses.

Que vous dire de la vue, si ce n'est que c'est magnifique et que c'est une des plus belles choses que nous n'ayons jamais vu ?!!!
Franchement, allez-y sans crainte et profitez de chaque instant.

Le vol a duré 1h10 et le prix est clairement justifié.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: We took a tour with Alan from the South Rim to Glen Canyon where we continued with Smooth Water Rafting on the Colorado River.  He picked us up at Lee's Ferry and we continued our tour back to the South Rim.  Alan was a wealth of knowledge and our trip was perfect.  He is an awesome tour guide; we learned so much and his pleasant and courteous personality is a gift.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: We were initially a bit disappointed when the helicopter tours were booked out and opted for a fixed-wing Highlights tour instead. Good move! We saw much more of the canyon when we did a helicopter tour a few years ago, and loved every minute of it. The staff - both on the phone, at the counter and the aircrew - are fantastic. Without exception, they are courteous, friendly and very helpful.  I would have no hesitation whatsoever in recommending this tour - well done Scenic!!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: We were booked for a tour to the south rim but because of the shut down we couldn't go. Scenic airline were brilliant and altered our tour to fly to the west rim which was still open. The whole experience was incredible and very well organised. Many thanks
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
Seeing the Grand Canyon from the air during a 40 minute journey in a small aircraft was exhilarating to say the least, plus it gave you a real sense as to how big it actually is. At 10 miles long and 270 miles wide it is enormous.
A word of advice though. Try to do it on a still day. When we did it the wind was gusty and the plane bobbed about quite a bit!!!! Not for those with tender stomachs !!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: We decided to spring for the Canyon River Adventure as part of our western US National Parks tour and were so glad we did!!  It was a long day (12 hrs) but so worth it.  It began with a dawn flight over and through the Grand Canyon - awesome colors and views!!  Next came Antelope Canyon - a little known treasure on an Indian reservation.  This narrow walk-thru canyon is filled with spectacular colored rock and there are no words to express it.  Finally, we had a motorized raft ride down the Colorado River from Glen Canyon dam to Lee's Landing.  No serious rapids on this section of the river but prepare to get wet on the smaller "riffles."  This trip was worth every penny so don't err on the side of cheap.  Book it!!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Do it, do it!! Incredible service and great tour!
Review Text:
I am terrified of flying and was really dreading the Grand Canyon tour.
As we drove to Boulder airport I was becoming more and more terrified. As I walked into the airport a lovely lady who worked there greeted us and I started crying I was that scared. She was absolutely lovely she asked me if I am scared flying. I informed her I was and I was not sure if I could go ahead with it. She said this happens to a lot of people and if I go and check in and have a seat she will come back and have a chat with me.

After I checked in she came back, sat down next to me, explained that the plane is very safe, the pilots are fully qualified, if the conditions aren't safe they won't fly etc. She was so lovely, she gave me a hug and some vouchers for a free drink and a souvenir photo. I felt so much more at ease just by someone talking to me and I am SO glad I went through with it.

I did not get the lady's name during my mini meltdown but I thank her from the bottom of my heart. I did the tour on Saturday 5th October and arrived at the airport very early in the morning before sunrise.

We did the skywalk and had lunch overlooking the Grand Canyon. I was blown away. One of the true wonders of the world. No photos can do it justice.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
We thoroughly enjoyed our tour which only cost about $150 which we thought was very good value.
Hotel pick up/drop off service was handy, but very time consuming. Our one hour flight turned into a 5 hour excursion.
Can definately recommend the sunset tour time - the setting sun made the desert and canyon look amazing.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Great tour of South Rim - Transportation from airport needs work
Review Text:
My wife and I plus three other family members took the Grand Canyon Connoisseur trip from Las Vegas to the South Rim of the Grand Canyon on September 30th and had a great trip. We were picked up on time on the Strip, transported to the Boulder City Airport and then flew to the South Rim of the Grand Canyon Nat'l Park. Excellent box lunch was provided and we were bused to several viewing points in the Grand Canyon Village, where we spent 2 1/2 hours. Both the flight and bus trip within the National Park were narrated for key points. We had a great pilot and very smooth trip on the 70 minute flight each way. The Grand Canyon South Rim is breathtaking and something that everyone should try to see in person.

The problem after the return to the Boulder City airport is there were no representatives from Grand Canyon Tours at the airport to insure you got assigned on a shuttle bus back to Las Vegas. It took us 2 1/2 hours to get back from the Airport, which is normally only a 40 minute trip. Better work and staffing by Scenic Airlines/Grand Canyon Tours at Boulder City Airport would make this a 5 star trip.

Tip to Travellers - Make sure you get a Bus Pass at the Transportation Desk immediately upon your return to Boulder City Airport for the included free shuttle back to the Vegas hotels.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: Super ervaring! Ik vond het geweldig vanaf het moment dat je incheckt totdat je weer naar buiten loopt. Fijne ontvangst door een hele vriendelijke mevrouw aan de balie. Inchecken...wegen...boarden...en we kregen gelukkig onze window seats! Inclusief nederlands gesproken geluid op onze koptelefoon. De vlucht duurde 45min, tijdens de vlucht informatie over (het ontstaan van) de Grand Canyon, afgewisseld door muziek. Vooraf wordt er nog een leuke foto gemaakt van jou met de piloot en het vliegtuigje en je bent toerist dus natuurlijk koop je die bij terugkomst. Tip: vanaf thuis al boeken!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Longer day than expected with lots of waiting around.
Review Text: I think the only way to see the Grand Canyon is to fly, either by plane or helicopter. We didnt fancy a 14hr bus tour and for the extra price I definately think the flight was worth it even though there was a lot of waiting around. We were picked up at 6am for a 8am flight, it took an hour to drive out to their airstrip in Boulder City and then had an hour to wait for our flight. All seemed to run smoothly until it was time to board our returning flight at 12.15pm, it was such a schmozzle the pilots didnt know who was on what flight, They let people that had been on later morning flights board planes before those that had been on earlier ones. Needless to say we ended up having to wait another 2hrs before we could finally board our flight.To top this off, when returning back to Boulder City we had to wait another 40mins for our transfers back to Las Vegas. Lots of waiting around with this tour that could have been avoided if the company was a bit more organised. Would recommend it but only because it's better then the alternative bus tour.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Great value for a Grand Canyon 'must'.
Review Text:
Booked the Grand Discovery plane tour (through Papillon) for a 9am flight. The check-in staff and pilot were friendly and we boarded with minimal fuss. The tour itself was a 45 minute flight, and we had an 8-seater plane. The high wings and seat placing meant everyone gets an uninterrupted view, which I thought was brilliant! The guided audio tour is fine, with some information interspersed between music - you can choose not to listen though.

The views are stunning and the plane tour, which was the cheapest flight over the Canyon we could find, was an excellent way of seeing the Canyon on a lower budget.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: Vol dans un petit avion de 8 places ou tout le monde a son hublot, génial ! Accueil très sympatique, photo avec le pilote et c est parti pour 1 heure de pur bonheur.  Vues a couper le souffle, grandioses, magiques. Tout le monde est équipe d un casque avec commentaires dans la langue de votre choix. On en a vraiment pour notre argent. A faire impérativement si on va au grand canyon
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
Checked in at 8:15am for a 9:00am flight. They weighed us and gave us our seat assignments. 1 seat on the left side, 2 seats on the right side of the aircraft (Twin Otter). I asked about getting a seat on the left side (heard it was better). The agent said that because we had children, we needed to be seated next to them, thus, we'd be on the right side. I was disappointed, but hey, it sounds reasonable to me.

The crew offer a picture in front of the airplane before boarding. On board, we are given a quick safety brief and shown where the barf bags are. They have headset over which a guided tour is played during the flight.

The right side of the airplane is just fine for viewing the canyon and surrounding areas. I certainly didn't feel cheated. The windows are big and you can see out of either side. Note: if you are seat in row 4, the wing strut will be in the middle of your field of view. Not a deal breaker, but something to consider.

The canned tour was of poor quality and after about twenty minutes, I just took the headsets off so I could speak to my son.

Great flight and nice landing.

They try to sell you the photo at the end of the tour. It is a decent photo of your family surrounded by a collage of Grand Canyon images. Not my cup of tea, so we didn't spend the $20.

IMPORTANT: On your online reservation email, read the terms and conditions! You must call prior to showing up to RE-confirm that you will be there, otherwise you could be wait-listed! Our flight wasn't full, but I would have been pretty upset if it was! Luckily, I was rereading the driving directions when I saw that little gem.

We went for the morning flight in order to avoid some of the bumps. That went reasonably well, although the air conditioning did smell of exhaust that started to give us headaches after an :45.

All in all, we are really glad we did it.

Don't forget to tip your pilots! They are trained professionals working very hard for not a lot of money.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: 360 views of the GC!  (But still very loud in a helicopter...)
Review Text:
Did this with a friend who was visiting the States from Asia. Had been to the Grand Canyon myself while in high school (stayed in a cabin with family at the North Rim -- and was still able to enjoy sitting on the veranda overlooking the Canyon, even though we stayed in a cabin, and not at the much pricier NPS Lodge). Even though my h.s. memories of the GC were wonderful, *nothing* could have prepared me for the amazing views of the Canyon from that helicopter! Absolutely LOVED it!

4-star rating, and not 5-star, due to the unbelievably LOUD noise level of the chopper's blades -- even though all 10-12 of the passengers were wearing Scenic Airlines' "special headphones" (supposedly to "block out noise"!). They didn't play music through our headphones on our trip -- but *maybe* after Scenic heard that not all passengers wanted gorgeous views with all that racket they added the music to help "cover" -- a nice idea.

We each paid for a RT ticket -- from the more local Las Vegas airport to the GCA ("Grand Canyon Airport"), stayed overnight, but the flight left very early in the morning, so there really wasn't much time for hiking, etc. Only wish we had taken video cameras, like many of the other passengers had done!

Review Title: Be prepared for lot of waiting around at the canyon
Review Text: We went on the plane-helicopter-riverboat tour. This tour was not very well organised at all. The individual aspects on their own were great but put together as a tour, it was poorly organised and we were left extremely disappointed.  Everything up until we reached the canyon airport was great, once we got there it was a complete shambles. We waited for half hour to then be told the helicopter wasnt ready (there werent enough on deck by the sounds). So we were told to take the bus up to the viewing point and get our lunch - it was 9:30am. We were told to be back on the bus at 10:15 to come back to west rim air strip for our helicopter. We had less than one hour to do it all. Even the staff said it wasnt realistic and as it happened one of our group members missed out on lunch as there was a queue for the bathroom. We rushed, got back on time and still had to wait another 20mins for our chopper. Get to the boat platform, queue up again to wait for the boat. 20mins later, finally get on a boat. Nowhere to sit at any waiting places, there were some seats but the number of people far exceeded the number of seats. Spent most of our time at Grand Canyon in an airport or waiting around. The staff tried hard and were very friendly but the system organisation is not good. Papillon operated our helicopter and i would fly direct to GC with them from Boulder City if I could do it over again.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
We took the plane ride over the canyon, antelope canyon tour and river raft trip.
It was worth every penny.
The breakfast and lunch provided were more than enough food and packed with lots of options to please everyone.
The plane ride gave me an opportunity to get some great pictures and views of the river not accessible from the rim of the canyon
Antelope Canyon left me speechless....I took 50 pictures.
The river raft trip was wonderful and our guide John was awesome. Everybody on our raft really enjoyed themselves. It was a very safe easy trip. Only got a few splashes....but we asked for it. The water was ice cold, 46 degrees I think, but we all jumped in when we stopped for a rest.

Review Text:
My family and I just did Grand Canyon Indian Adventure and Skywalk. In fact, we are still waiting here for a bus to take us back to our hotel- almost 8 hours from when they picked us up this morning (and the tour was only supposed to go 7 hours). By the time we get back to our hotel, we will have spent 5 hours waiting or being shuttled with only 3.5 hours of actual Grand Canyon experience.

The airplane ride was beautiful, but the plane was not air conditioned as advertised - an important fact in July heat waves. An intake fan does keep the air moving, but that's all. The pot roast style lunch at Guano Point was unedible although the location was breathtaking.

The Grand Canyon itself is beyond words, and I am glad my children were able to see it. But we felt deceived by the advertising - expecting a much more personal experience. Maybe the helicopter tours are different, but this was not what we were looking for at all.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Awesome trip less the waiting time
Review Text: My hubby and I decided not to miss the Grand Canyon since we are already in Vegas. The trip was booked very last minute, just 1-2 days before when we passed by a store along the strip. We just walked in and was greeted by a friendly lady at the counter. We were initially thinking of going on a coach which cost around US160-170 but that would have taken us abt 15+ hrs for the entire trip. Review Title: TRATAR DE ELEGIR UNA EXCURSION COMPLETA
Review Text:

Review Text:
Our family did the Canyon River Adventure over the Memorial Day holiday weekend. It was a very long, but fun day. It was exactly 12 hours from the moment our plane left the ground until we arrived back at the airport. My husband and I had no problem getting out 10 and 15 year old daughters to bed that night. In fact we all slept 12 hours we were so tired. The tour was well organized, and worth every cent. Upon check in at the airport we were served a huge boxed breakfast, too much to eat at once. We took the extra leftover items for snacks later. High energy adventure requires food to fuel the body, which they provided plenty. Bring your cameras, sunscreen, something to cover your mouth/nose while exploring Antelope Canyon, secured sun hats and protective sunglasses that will help prevent sand in your eyes. When boarding the airplane, try to get a seat on the left side because most of the canyon is visible from the left side.
I suggest protective lens for your camera during the walk through Antelope Canyon, as sand can ruin a camera easily. I'd also wear a quality face mask or a scarf to prevent inhaling the dust. Despite being told you won't get wet on the raft trip, you can expect to get wet. We got soaked, but it felt good. Mostly everyone slept most of the bus ride back.
