Review Title: Superb aerial views of the Canyon
Review Text:
We went on the Visionary Air Tour. The pick-up from the hotel was punctual and the check-in was efficient. The flight itself which was a bit over an hour was great although there was some turbulence, which was expected given the size of the plane.

Review Title: Great scenery but the customer service needs some improvement
Review Text:
Overall I'm glad I did this ride. It is a wonderful 70 minute flight into one of nature's great wonders. Grand Canyon Airlines runs this particular trip out of Boulder but they will pick up at your Vegas hotel. A nice plus.

Once you get there it is a bit of a busy environment because they're running helicopter tours out of the small terminal too. But it is fairly straightforward. You get a pink or blue sticker that tells you which group you're with.

They are very keen to herd you around like cattle at this point and I guess with the volume they do I see why. But they also insist on taking your pic with the pilot whether you want it or not. This is supposedly an optional thing you buy for $20 as a souvenir when you come back.

Why is this done? I say it's so they can have a photo record of you. Because if it was optional you could just hop on the plane without doing this if you didn't want to have a pic. They should just tell you that upfront. That it's for i.d. and record keeping purposes! Minus some points for this.

And after your flight takes of you'll find that the Grand Canyon is going to amaze, overwhelm and just plain have your jaw dropping once you are flying over it. They spend quite a bit of time over the various parts of the canyon and there is an audio message you can listen to for background info.

Some bad news for single travellers. You are likely to end up over the wing strut which basically blocks all decent views for photos down into the scenery. Instead of putting me in a single row seat up front they went and stuck me over the strut.

They could have put either one of two families with kids across an entire row and let me have a decent window seat as a solo traveller. The child behind me wasn't even interested in the view and really wasted her window seat. Yes I know they have to weight and balance these airplanes but I'm not a large man. Minus some more points for that.

When you come back you hop on their shuttle back to town. But in the ensuing blabber about telling you how to walk back to the terminal, they DON"T tell you have to check back in at the desk to get a boarding pass for the shuttle!!! Inexcusable.

I was left wondering what I should do and just thought I'd hop on a shuttle going back, and one of their shuttle drivers rudely told me I couldn't ride on a bus going back to Vegas because I didn't have a bus pass!

Not a good ending to a pleasant flight. Overall this attraction lost a lot of points because of these simple glitches that could have easily been prevented from happening... and I rate it as average to poor for customer service issues.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
We took an all day "air, river float & canyon combination tour". As of July 2012 they called it the Grand Canyon River Adventure. 5:45 am to about 6:30 pm. A very looong day. We enjoyed the air tour. We enjoyed the river float in Glen Canyon. We hated almost everything to do with the rest of the tour.

Our tour started at the south rim airport with a small plane air tour of the canyon. We enjoyed it although in retrospect we also decided that a helicopter might have been preferable. But we saw the canyon from the air and that's really cool.

The airplane took us to the Page, AZ airport where we were told we would be picked up for a tour of Antelope Canyon, perhaps the best of the slot canyons in the area. We waited about 25 minutes, which was far too long. Like they didn't know when to expect us?

Eventually we were picked up at the airport by an extremely rude driver. He almost left half the tour because when he called for us we didn't hear him and evidently that pissed him off. Great attitude. We were loaded on human trailers that had no shocks for a very uncomfortable ride to Antelope Canyon. The canyon itself was interesting although our guide didn't have much to tell us except where to take pictures. Then we're loaded back onto the uncomfortable trailers and dropped off in town at a hiking goods/gift shop retail location to wait for our ride to the river float.

Here's where it got really irritating. We waited almost 1 1/2 hours at the store and I was getting angrier by the minute. Far too many people milling around in a very small space. The clerks in the store clearly unhappy that we were all in the store, but there was nowhere else to go. My family was asked twice to wait outside and I refused both times. It was horribly hot outside. July in the desert. Apparently, the wait was to allow us lots and lots of time to buy things. That always irritates me and it really irritated me on that occasion. Finally the buses arrive, we're issued box lunches and off we go. As I said the river float itself was enjoyable. Glen Canyon is a very slow current so it's a float - not a white water adventure. Nonetheless, we had a fun guide and the float itself was fun.

Then off the rafts and onto buses to be driven all the way back to the south rim - about a 90 minute drive if I remember correctly. That would have been fine except....WE HAD TO STOP AGAIN FOR ANOTHER BUYING OPPORTUNITY!!!. We're all tired and ready to be back at the hotel, but we're forced to waste another 45 minutes at the Indian tourist junk store on the way back !! ARRRGGGG!

Save yourself the frustration. The indian tribe that operates the Antelope Canyon tour does a TERRIBLE job. Not worth it and those we encountered were unprofessional and rude. Far too much of your day is wasted in worthless gift shops, and they are not very friendly in those gift shops. If you want an air tour, take an air tour by itself. If you want to float Glen Canyon, do that. It's fun. Do not take one of these all day combination tours. Trust me.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Maybe not as thrilling as a helicopter ride, but cheaper and safer!
Review Text:
We chose the GCA Visionary tour based primarily on safety (helicopter accidents @GC are much more common than fixed wing ones) and secondly on price (its a lot cheaper than a helicopter, and you can find a 2-1 voucher on the internet if you look, which works out slightly cheaper than the online discounted price per person).

Firstly I should say that everything ran smoothly. Pickup from hotel was on time, only a short wait at Boulder City Airport and we were off. From my seat I could see the cockpit and assessed (as a former pilot) the pilot and co-pilot (the latter was in charge of the aircraft whilst airborne) to be very professional.The return trip to LV was also prompt.

I very much enjoyed the tour. Alas my partner kept her eyes front for the whole duration because she was too scared to look out of the window! We chose the early morning set off, but I suspect that a later flight might give better lighting for photos and videos.

Okay, the flight could have gone further along the canyon. And whilst you get a good view, it is perhaps not as great as with a helicopter. But if you are short on time and have a limited budget, but still want to experience the Grand Canyon, then this is a good option.

Review Title: Best views of the Grand Canyon by Plane.
Review Text:
We arrived in the grand canyon area just after lunch, we had pre booked the beautiful Grand Motel, upon checking in to the motel we asked about the best flight tour company to take us over the canyon. the staff were very helpful giving us a number of brochures on companies that offered both helicopter & plane tours. We took a look at the opinions & decided to choose the Grand Canyon Airlines, Grand Discovery Tour. We walked back to the reception of the motel & asked if they could organise the tour for two adults & two children for the first tour available in the morning of the next day? She asked if I would like to wait & she would do it right away, I said fantastic! Upon contacting the company she said that we where booked on the 8am flight in the morning & gave us directions to the Grand Canyon Airport where we would be departing, told us to be there by 7.30am. Turned out a great place to stay as it was so close to both the airport & only a couple of mile to the National park entrance.
So up at 6.30 am, ,got dressed & headed to the Grand Canyon Airport to catch the early 8am flight out over the canyon, we arrived on time & we the reservations as fine & the staff handled the arrival in a professional manner, all safety precaution we followed, weighing everyone & all luggage going on the flight. We where hoping to get a window seat to get the clearest photo opportunities, turned out we only have 4 others on our flight, so all folks on the plane had a window seat. The normal safety checks from one of the pilots to all on board, a quick verbal of how to set up your head set & of to the runway. We had a smooth take off & good weather as we flew out across the canyon in a 16 seater plane for some amazing views of the whole Grand Canyon incredible experience. We had a narrated tour that lasted about 45 mins, We got some wonderful photos & video footage, it really did feel like we where in the air for such a long time, awesome stuff, this is a great way to see the canyon. You do get to see much more of the canyon from the plane & the weather was fine & clear. After the flight we headed back to the Grand Hotel for breakfast & then of to the National park to experience the canyon from the ground with a trek down a trail. Very happy with the Grand Canyon Airlines company & the tour we choose. Cost $120 per adult $100 per child. Good value for money.

Review Text:
When my bank saw the Grand Canyon Airlines name on my charges, it issued a fraud alert and blocked any further purchases. I thought this was a mistake on their part, but perhaps this action was warranted, as we feel the services promised by 'Grand Canyon Adventures'
were not the services delivered. Far from it. We saw very little of the Grand Canyon and far too much, 5.5 hours in fact, of the airport gift shop, helioport gift shop, and parking lot.

1. Of the 8 hours invested in this 'adventure' we spent 2.5 hours in flight, .25 hours or less in the helicopter hovering over one area of the south rim of the Grand Canyon and one hour at the Grand Canyon National Park. Actually 45 minutes viewing the Grand Canyon from the ground, we spent 15 minutes consuming our pitiful excuse for a lunch. The balance, an estimated 5.5 hours was spent...waiting...waiting...waiting... at the airport, heliport, or on the bus/shuttle in the parking lot of the airport, helioport, etc. etc.

2. On the first flight we were wedged into the small aircraft like sardines. I am a fairly small woman, as was my companion, an average sized man, so it should have been spacious for smaller folks. It wasn't. No air to speak of, certainly not air conditioned for comfort as advertised, it was horrendously hot and uncomfortable. We could not breath, got an excruciating headache from it and nausea ensured, although we managed not to throw up. And I have never been air sick, never, even in an ultralight. The views and photography were obstructed by the rotar blades, and of course, other people blocking the windows.
The refitting of the aircraft may have benefited their profit margin but it is detrimental to the passengers.

3. During the helicopter flight I was wedged between two large men, one a total stranger, my petite frame squeezed so tight my lungs barely had room to expand. Needless to say it was embarrassing and humiliating. I am a petite female by the way, and don't appreciate the indignity of having any strange man's body that intimate with mine, thanks. This advertisement is false, actually, this was not the view. Most of the time on the helicopter was spent flying to the Grand Canyon, not over the Grand Canyon. We hovered over the same portion, turning to see the same view from a different perspective before we flew back to the heliport.

4. During the flight back, we were again crammed into an overcrowded plane, did not sit with my traveling companion at all. There were tiny windows in the plane, not the 'panoramic windows' promised, not much of a view on our side of the plane, and again, nausea ensued, difficulty breathing. Too late to back out when we saw the plane, it was our ride back to the airport...and more waiting. Again, stuffed into too small of a space.

5. When we asked about the two viewing points we were suppose to be shuttled to at the park, we were told that yes, the brochures says that, but it will depend on the helicopter schedule, shuttle schedule, etc. So we walked to one viewing point, never saw the other, had to hurry back to the shuttle as we were warned we would miss our plane ride home. No one seemed to know who we needed to speak to about the issue, and we were shifted from one person to another.

6. Should perhaps drive to the canyon, do the helicopter ride from there. Could perhaps have more alternatives if you aren't trapped in a situation you have already paid for.

Review Title: Great way to see the Grand Canyon and Skywalk
Review Text:
When organising our trip to Las Vegas, Alaska and Canada top priority was given to having the best possible day trip to see the Grand Canyon and Skywalk. With the help of our travel agent, we decided on Scenic Airlines 'Grand Canyon, Indian Adventure - Helicopter, Boat and Skywalk Tour'.
We were picked up from our Hotel (Signature at MGM Grand) at 4.50am by their shuttle and after picking up a few other guests, were on our way to Boulder Airport. After processing and grouping there, we climbed aboard the 18 seat aircraft for our trip to the Grand Canyon Airport where we were given a boxed lunch to take with us. (Nothing to write home about but it was sufficient to keep us going). This is a great flight, flying over the Hoover Dam, Lake Mead and the West Rim.
We were then taken by bus to the Skywalk area, and did the walk ! The views were just majestic. After the set time, we were then bussed to another viewing area, after which we were taken back to the Grand Canyon Airport to board our Helicopter for the descent into the Canyon. Wow, what a buzz this flight is. We are now down in the canyon, walked down to the Colarado river (via a track and stairways) for our pontoon boat excursion. It was so quiet and surreal. Being summer time, by the time we returned back to the helicopter pad from the river it was 42deg C. After a short wait, we were back into the helicopter and back up to the airport. This is such an amazing flight, and should not be missed.
We then flew back to Boulder Airport in the 18 seat aircraft, and returned to Vegas by their shuttle from Boulder.
We found the whole process to be very well organised and professionally planned. It was not a cheap trip any any means, but if you want to do things properly then you have to pay for it. It was a once in a lifetime event for us Aussies and one we will never forget.

Review Title: Spectacular day, varied and accessible to nearly any age or ability
Review Text:
Instead of hours on a mule to reach the canyon floor, we are darn glad we opted to do this. It is an adventure.

For departure, go to Grand Canyon Airport (not heliport!) We recommend sitting on the right side of the airplane for the great views of the canyons; plan to bring extra food, water and reading material or games. Plenty of toilets available on the entire trip. The river is easy but it is spectacular. Young children might find the ride home too long unless they are nappers. People with difficulty walking could enjoy the day. The outfitters will accommodate wheelchairs as long as the chair can be folded up and there is someone to push the chair. A chair would not be great in Antelope Canyon, however. This is a flat, easy walk but the floor is sand - very tough on wheels. But the flight and the raft (and fun short bus ride from Page to Glen Canyon Dam) are fabulous.

Our river guide, Meghan (?), was splendid - a biologist, historian, naturalist and fine storyteller. We loved this portion and were never bored even though there are no rapids here. You just float past magnificent and varied scenery. Bring extra batteries, binoculars would be fun, dress in layers - we had three seasons in one outing. You definitely need sun protection (even in April!) and the hikes are so easy you need no special footwear.

Once on Colorado River there are three stops, one is a splendid sandy beach. You might to wear like a swim suit or fast dry clothes on a hot day. Each stop has toilets.

There are some waits throughout the day and a very long ride home on a motorcoach from Lee's Ferry back to GC Airport but you will see how the Navaho people live . Their reservation borders the road home. You can shop for fine Navaho art and crafts at the Cameron Trading Post Galley on the ride home. Just avoid the junk in the large, also junky, gift shop. The food options at the Trading Post are bleak - mostly junk food.

Trips can be cancelled due to weather issues so be sure to confirm the day before and understand if winds get too strong you may not be able to go. Both days before and after our trip were cancelled.

The return trip takes you into the National Park at the east entrance, Desert View. However, the bus home does not stop at any of the lookouts once in the park. But you will be glad, ready to get back to your car and your hotel.

Though the trip seems expensive it is worth every penny. It was a great deal more fun and interesting than sitting on a mule.

Review Title: Canyon River Adventure – Plane, 4x4 Vehicle, River Raft, Motor Coach
Review Text:
I booked the “Canyon River Adventure” tour directly with Grand Canyon Airlines but you can also book thru Papillon Grand Canyon Helicopters, GrandCanyon.com, or Xanterra Parks & Resorts. This tour departs from the Grand Canyon Airport in Tusayan (8 miles south of Grand Canyon Village / Grand Canyon South Rim).

This comprehensive tour is operated by the partnership of 3 companies:
GRAND CANYON AIRLINES - flight over canyon in fixed wing 19-seat Vistaliner plane with over-sized windows;
ANTELOPE SLOT CANYON TOURS – four-wheel drive vehicle tour to Antelope Canyon;
COLORADO RIVER DISCOVERY - 15-mile smooth water float trip on a river raft, beginning at Glen Canyon Dam and ending at Lee’s Ferry.

At the end of the full-day excursion, a motor coach returns you back to Grand Canyon Airport.

Tour Description and Video: http://youtu.be/_Qi2Lpemuyc

Tips for hot days: Sunblock, wide brim hat, a small towel or bandana to soak in river and wrap around neck. Store all electronic devices in a waterproof bag. My boyfriend’s cell phone and iTouch were both ruined by a splash of river water on his backpack. The seats and floor of the raft can also become wet with small puddles of water.

If you are prone to motion sickness, consider taking a half tablet of Bonine (or similar antiemetic) before the plane tour. Wind gusts over the canyon can occur, making the ride intermittently bumpy.

The 2-mile journey on the 4x4 vehicle to Antelope Canyon is very bumpy and dusty. You will travel over an unpaved road in thick sand. Those with back problems and contact lense wearers should beware. Antelope Canyon is a natural marvel and a photographer’s oasis.

My husband and I booked a Visionary Flight from Grand Canyon Airlines, its the cheapest flight. Plan on about 4 hours round trip from the hotel. We checked in, waited about 30 minutes, just long enough to have a cup of coffee and a donut, then were loaded onto another bus, and driven out to the tarmac.

NOTE: there are very clean rest rooms in the airport, but NONE on the plane!

Each person/couple poses with the pilot, then receives a seat assignment and boards. The plane seats around 20 people, single person on one left, 2 side-by-side on the right. Windows are oversized for good viewing. headsets are available for up to 4 languages, our flight included English, Korean, and Swedish, each on its own channel. So, off we go, short flight to Boulder Dam, then over Lake Meade, and finally to the Grand Canyon. Awesome, awe inspiring, there are just not words to describe its majesty viewed from the air. Total in-air time was about 60 minutes. Then we landed. You can purchase your photo with the pilot for $20, spend the extra $9 for the video; this is a very slick, professional video of the entire length of the Colorado River, about 60 minutes long, very very well done. Then we received a token, went outside, boarded a shuttle. We were driven to a transfer point, got off and transferred to another shuttle, and driven back to the hotel. About 3.5 hours total.

This is not a cheap trip, its going to cost about $150 per person (around $125 plus tax). The bus tour is around 10 hours total trip, and not much cheaper (about $100/person without tax). However, if you do the GCA tour in the morning, you are back in Vegas by lunch, and still have the entire afternoon and evening to enjoy. For $25 more per person, we felt that CGA was the better route, and it was.

Review Title: No Trip to Las Vegas Would Be Complete Without It
Review Text:
Having booked a week in Las Vegas over the 4th July weekend, one of our top priorities was to get to see the Grand Canyon. We originally planned on hiring a car and driving there, but were put off by the lengthy drive and the idea of a whole day cooking together in the car !
Instead, we decided to look at our options for taking a flight over the Canyon. Taking our place in the human mass that ebbs and flows up and down the Strip, we were occasionally cornered by sales or timeshare agents trying to persuade us to part with more of our overdraft (!) in exchange for a variety of trips, shows and events. We quickly established that booking a flight through these agents was going to cost a minimum of $130 each (around £80 in real money) for a plane trip, and substantially more for a helicopter ride. We also learned the hard way, that it's sometimes difficult to extract yourself from the clutches of these agents, if they get even the slightest sniff of possibility that you might take your wallet or your credit card out. So if you intend speaking to them, you have to be prepared to walk away if you don't want what they're selling !

Once we'd established the 'ball-park' cost of a trip, we returned to our hotel and accessed the internet to compare prices direct. Keeping to our budget, we wanted a short plane ride which wouldn't take up all of our day. After some searching, we found GrandCanyonAirlines.com who have a broad spectrum of both helicopter and airplane options available. Their website is easy to use and their prices are far better than most. We booked 2 tickets online for $94 each (around £60), opting for the early morning (6am) flight. Be warned though - the website allows you to check flight availability for the next day but it doesn't tell you until AFTER you've made your selections, that you have to book at least 3 days in advance !?!?! So don't leave it until the end of your holiday to book in. Having negotiated this minor hurdle, we then discovered that our pick-up time would be at an ungodly 4am ! Not the easiest time in the morning to rise after a night of Mojitos and Margueritas ! !

Anyway, on the day, our pick-up was running 10 or 15 minutes late (no big deal) and after collecting four other couples, the drive to Boulder City airstrip took around 40 minutes. The set up there is pretty good and certainly better than I imagined it might be. They have a fairly new terminal building with a small coffee shop / gift store, and enough seating for most. Each passenger books in and is then weighed, to calculate distribution around the airplane cabin. This was particularly pleasing as it made a mockery of those who had raced off the bus to be first in line, shouldering children and elderly folk out of the way to get the best seats - I'm joking of course but there was a stampede to be first in line ! Outside on the apron were numerous helicopters and around the corner sat the airplanes. Lots of people were arriving from different places for a number of early flights. Unfortunately for us, only 4 of the 8 passengers booked on our plane had managed to drag themselves out of bed for the pick-up, and our flight was cancelled. This is something else to be wary of, although you have no control over it. If they don't have the minimum number on the day, the flight is scrubbed. We were offered alternative flights and chose to return next morning at a slightly later time (so we could get more sleep ! !).

Our pick-up next morning was more eventful - Running late again with another family already on the bus, we were then delayed a further 20 minutes at our hotel while we waited for members of said family to visit the restrooms ! What it is exactly that takes 20 minutes, I'll never know ! ! ! However, this is another drawback of these trips and you should be prepared for the possibility that your pick-up may run very late. It clearly caused some concern with those waiting further along the Strip to be collected. Nonetheless, we still arrived at Boulder in time so there was less time sitting around.

So to the flight. The plane was small and cosy with large viewing windows. The crew were very friendly and accommodating. We had headsets that alternated between playing an audio travel guide with useful information on the area, and a cheesy soundtrack that I reckon was taken from "Blazing saddles" ! The flight was nice and smooth (taking into account the odd airpocket that wouldn't constitute turbulence, but which still caused my other half to attempt to surgically remove my left bicep, using only her fingernails and her teeth ! !) And the Grand Canyon itself... What can I possibly say that far better writers than I, havn't already said...? It was an experience we'll never forget. It was utterly magnificent. It's impossible to convey the sheer scale and magnitude and it was so humbling to fly over it, through it and around it. Driving to the rim would never have afforded such views, so taking the plane ride was money well spent. It was a fabulous journey which also took in the Hoover Dam and it's new road bridge, as well as Lake Mead.

Would we recommend Grand Canyon Airlines? Definitely.
Would we fly with them again? Absolutely. In a helicopter next I think !
What should you take? Cameras, spare batteries and memory card, cash (for the coffee shop / gift store), sunglasses, water (it can get pretty stuffy if the bus is full).

Review Text:
We had an amazing experience with Scenic Airlines last week (November 2008).

We took the overnight tour - which included an early pick-up from the hotel (5am!!!), an amazing and incredibly smooth flight at 6:40am from Boulder City airport to the South Rim of the Grand Canyon), a drop off at a viewing point, a rather delicious buffet lunch at a hotel in Tusayan, a visit to an Imaxx theatre to see a film about the Grand Canyon, and then a further drop off at the Bright Angel viewing point (which was very close to out hotel - The Maswik Lodges). We were able to see the Sunset, and in the following morning we had an option to get up and see the Sunrise too (a bus picked us up at 6:30am to take us to a suitable viewing point). This whole trip was excellently organised and run by a group of exrtremely affable and interesting tour guides.

I can't reccommend this trip enough! It was one of the very few companies that offered flights to the South Rim of the Canyon, with an overnight stay in the park itself. Well worth the money! The tour was the right balance of laid back and very organised (none of that hassled 'herded' feeling - and you didn't feel that they were continuously pushing you into over priced gift shops). I felt that we were given the opportunity to get a real flavour of the area - and the guides were very informative (some passengers took a free shuttle bus to see yet more viewing points - and were given the information to do so by Rick, the guide).

We managed to book the tour via a travel agent in the Planet Hollywood hotel - a kiosk right in the Miracle Mile shopping centre (just as you go through from the casino into the shopping centre).

(p.s. We managed to see plenty of wildlife at the Canyon - deer, wild pigs and chipmunks, and there were some nice gift shopping opportunities - but this was in no way shoved down your throat). We also managed to get a very nice evening meal from the Arizona Lodge amd a delicious breakfast from the Bright Angel hotel. The beers in the Bright Angel hotel were also very good... we sampled a few "Fat Tires" during our evening stay ;-)

Review Text:
We recently visited the Grand Canyon as our intended highlight on a three week USA West Coast trip. We researched Grand Canyon tours as thoroughly as possible, reading trip advisor, asking people etc.

We opted for flying to the Grand Canyon for a South Rim Connoisseur tour with Scenic Airlines which advertised extended viewing for about two or three hours-enough time to enjoy a meal, shops, see the Imax movie and ample time to explore the canyon!

We booked online-for a dawn pickup-it said our booking was successful and that that time was available. NO E-ticket arrived within 48 hours as stated so we rang up and were told a confirmation number was fine.

IN Las Vegas we realised that our time had been changed to a pickup at 11.40 for a 1.15 flight. We were then told that times are not guaranteed on the net!

We were picked up for our hotel-spent an hour waiting at Boulder airport before leaving with others -with same tour and other tour labels in all sorts of colours. On arrival at Canyon we were all on same bus-dropped off helicopter people who were then all mixed up again with other tours for a helicopter ride. Fuel surcharge of $25 each for lightweights a ripoff.

Meanwhile we were taken to a 45 minute Imax movie (meanwhile the real thing we want to see is there) .After that we sat on the bus for about 50 minutes to wait for the last of the helicopter people to arrive back.

We later discovered that we could have been driven to the Mather Point or another point to have a view but the driver felt we had to wait til all copter people had come back. A 30-40 minute look at Mather Point with a lot of people and then a brief 15 minute look from Bright Angel Point at about 6 pm at night. Had to take photos in a hurry before dark. Dark on thje way back and Japanese people got no view to match their commentary which had not been available on way up. Several of us were not happy at all-have asked for at least a partial refund with no success.

Scenic even asked the driver to extend the tour -impossible to consider doing effectively in the dark.

We felt like we were bandaids just to make up numbers for a tour that cost us $600 plus Aust dollars. Scenic Airlines wasted at least two hours of our precious time-just waiting for things to happen.
We came home disappointed with little feeling that we had even seen the Canyon-it would have been fine if no wasted time.

Review Text:
Aviso de antemano que ésta es una crítica muy detallada, por lo que puede resultar un poco pesada de leer, pero si buscar información para contratar una excursión en avioneta al Gran Cañón, con descenso en helicóptero, paseo en barca y comida, yo que tú no me perdería detalle ;)

Considerando tanto las críticas buenas como las malas, y después de comparar precios con todos los operadores de excursiones al Gran Cañón desde Las Vegas, me decidí por contratar con Scenic Airlines su "Grand Voyager Tour" (http://www.scenic.com/saws1gc_grand_voyager.htm).

Lo contraté con 1 mes de antelación desde su propia página web. En principio íbamos a ir 3 personas, y fue para los que reservé el viaje. Al tipo de cambio vigente en el momento de la compra (Junio 2008), las 3 personas salieron por 957$ = 616€, lo que son 205€ por persona, a lo que hay que sumar 20$ por persona en concepto de suplemento por combustible a pagar en destino. A los pocos minutos de realizar la compra recibes un correo electrónico con los detalles del pedido, y a las 24h aproximadamente envían el "e-ticket" con el número de confirmación, la hora y el lugar donde pasan a recogerte.

Destacar que el hecho de contratar en su web supone un ahorro mínimo aproximado de un 30% con respecto a los precios que ofrecen las mayoristas de viajes. Por ejemplo, Catai Tours ofrece esta excursión con Papillon Grand Canyon Helicopters por 302€ (página 21 folleto Estados Unidos y Canadá marzo 2007/marzo 2008)

Scenic deja clarísimo en su web y en los mails que envían tras la reserva, que es de vital importancia llamar el día antes del viaje a la central de reservas (número gratuito) para confirmar que por condiciones climáticas no se haya cancelado la excursión, la asistencia de los pasarejos y la hora y lugar de recogida el Las Vegas. Yo había solicitado hacer la excursión a primera hora de la mañana, de 6-8, para ver amanecer en el Gran Cañón, pero ya en el mail de confirmación me notificaron que nos recogerían a las 12:45pm para salir de Boulder City en avioneta al Gran Cañón a las 2:00pm. Ok, madrugón que nos ahorramos, cosa que nos vino genial para descansar de la paliza de ver hoteles la tarde/noche anterior. De no haberme convencido la hora, podía haber cancelado el viaje con la devolución del 100% del importe cobrado.

Por motivos laborales, uno de mis amigos tuvo que cambiar de planes en pleno viaje y no iba a poder llegar con nosotros a Las Vegas. Inmediatamente me puse en contacto con Scenic para cancelar la reserva de 1 de los 3 pasajeros que íbamos a ser. Tienen al menos una operadora que habla castellano. Aunque no sea la alegrái de la huerta, precisamente, fue muy profesional y resolvió todas mis dudas. Me dijeron que tardarían entre 2 y 3 semanas en realizar la devolución (reintegro en tarjeta de crédito), pero en vez de devolver el 100% descontaron 40$ en concepto de suplemento por carburante, 20$ por cada uno de los 2 pasajeros que sí íbamos a viajar. Como ya sabía que nos lo cobrarían al hacer el check-in, aceptamos sin problemas. Al cumplirse las 2 semanas comprobé que ya me habían hecho el reintegro en la tarjeta de crédito del importe indicado.

Ya en Las Vegas, un día antes de la excursión, llamé a Scenic para confirmar. Todo perfecto, pasajeros, horarios y excursión.

Nosotros nos alojamos en el Luxor Hotel & Casino, en el extremo sur de Las Vegas Blvd ("The Strip"). Como la furgoneta recorre de N-S el Strip recogiendo a los pasajeros en sus respectivos hoteles, cuanto más al sur estés, más tarde pasaran a recogerte, y menos tiempo pasarás en la furgoneta. Luxor y Excalibur fueron los 2 últimos hoteles de la ruta. De ahí al aeropuerto de donde sale la avioneta hay unos 35m, ya que salen desde el de Boulder City, no desde McCarran (el internacional que está frente al Luxor).

Es curioso que la furgoneta que nos recogió tuviera la serigrafía de Papillon (http://www.papillon.com/) teóricamente competencia de Scenic. A la llegada a la terminal del aeropuerto de Boulder City, hicimos check-in. Allí pesan a los pasajeros que no facilitaron su peso (en libras) al hacer la reserva por internet. Según la excursión que hayas contratado te ponen una pegatina de un tipo y color u otro. Así van llamando a la gente por grupos según su pegatina para embarcar en distintas avionetas. Te recomiendan comprar agua en la tienda de recuerdos (ojo, está cara, pero fresca).

Con respecto a la seguridad, comentaros que en el check-in nos comentaron que debido a las altas temperaturas registradas en el interior del cañón, rondando los 45ºC, existía la posibilidad de que se cancelara el descenso en helicóptero, y por extensión el paseo en barca, debido a que a partir de los 46ºC los helicópteros no despegan por motivos de seguridad. Nos ofrecieron cancelar la excursión sin ningún costo, cambiar la excursión por otra sin helicóptero (con Skywalk y/o con visitas en autobus) o esperar a ver si se cancelaba o no, en cuyo caso nos devolverían un porcentaje del viaje. Hay una chica que habla castellano, por lo que el idioma no es problema. Informados, y firmado un documento donde nos dábamos por enterados, decidimos arriesgarnos y dejarlo como estaba, con tan buena suerte que cuando aterrizamos en el west rim vimos helicópteros despegando sin problemas.

El vuelo en avioneta fue bastante bueno. El aparato es un De Havilland Twin Otters DHC-6 (http://www.scenic.com/saws1twinotter.htm). Antes de embarcar hacen fotos a todos los pasajeros por grupos con el capitán. Sientan a los pasajeros por grupos y pesos. Según las nacionalidades de los mismos, ponen narraciones para escuchar durante el vuelo con unos cascos con selección de canales (para seleccionar el idioma) y el volúmen.

Las vistas sobre el lago Mead y la presa Hoover son impresionantes. Los juegos de sombras sobre el desierto de Mohave son espectaculares. Nada más aterrizar separan a la gente por grupos, según la peganita que lleven, y a los del helicóptero les ponen un video de seguridad para el vuelo. Los helicópteros son de "Papillon Grand Canyon Helicopters" con 6 plazas (3+3 enfrentadas) +1 delante junto al piloto. Como íbamos 8 personas para la excursión con helicóptero y barco, primero despegó uno con 6 personas y luego otro con 2, con tan buena suerte de que esas dos fuimos mi amigo y yo. Un helicóptero para nosotros solos. Fue una auténtica pasada y no da nada de impresión. Dan un pequeño rodeo desde el aeropuerto para bajar por el cañón hasta un pequeño claro cerca del río. Allí te reciben un par de indios (el West Rim está en la reserva de los indios Hualapai) que amablemente de indican por dónde bajar a la orilla para tomar el bote. En el chiringo donde se resguardaban del sol vimos un termómetro marcando 45ºC, pero no teníamos tal sensación de calor, de hecho el calor era más agobiante en Las Vegas que en el Gran Cañón.

El paseo en barca es cutrecillo. Las vistas muy guapas, pero el paseo escaso. Básicamente consta de remotar el río unos 400 metros, parar el motor y dejar que la corriente lleve de vuelta la barca al embarcadero. Total 15-20 min. Mientras, el amable capitán, en un perfecto inglés de Ohio, cuenta historias del Cañón. Vuelta al improvisado helipuerto para volar de regreso al aeropuerto. Allí tomamos un autobús que nos llevó a Guano Point, donde hay un merendero donde te sirven el bufet (carne, pechuga de pollo, fajitas, algo parecido a compota de melocotón, un bollito, bebida y café) y tienes relativo poco tiempo para comer y hacerte las fotos que puedas. Las vistas son impresionantes, y preciosas al atardecer. Por la zona rondan cuervos sobrealimentados de las sobras de los bufets. Recomiendo no darles de comer.

A la hora fijada, vuelta al autobús. Es importantísimo estar puntual, porque si el autobús se va sin tí perderás el vuelo de regreso a Las Vegas, lo que supondría volver en autobús (aproximadamente 3h de viaje). Asíque recomiendo comer poco y rapidito para tener tiempo para hacer fotos, videos y admirar el paisaje, y así estar a tiempo esperando el bus, que es terrorificamente puntual!!

Nada más llegar al aeropuerto nos montamos en la misma avioneta en la que venimos, en los mismos asientos, y en 30 minutos estábamos de vuelta en Boulder City. En la terminal se pueden comprar por 15$ la foto con el capitán que te hicieron antes del viaje de ida. Subida a un autobús con sillones supercómodos de cuero y con pantallas de tv. Nos pusieron una película, lo que permite hacerse una idea de lo que tardan en dejar a los pasajeros en los hoteles más alejados, al norte del Strip. A nosotros nos dejaron los primeros en el Excalibur, aprovechando que está al lado del Luxor, y que tenían que bajar a más pasajerons para llevarles a hoteles más alejados en un bus con otra ruta.

Un 10 para la excursión, un 10 para la organización, un 10 para los pilotos, justitos los helicópteros y las avionetas, un poco cascadas por dentro, aunque nos comentaron que iban a adquirir nuevos modelos en breve (blablabla). Lo cierto es que en el aeropuerto del West Rim están haciendo una nueva terminal y una pista mayor, para permitir el aterrizaje y despegue de jets mayores, ya que hasta ahora sólo pueden utilizarlo pequeñas aeronaves de, como mucho, 21 pasajeros. Esto quiere decir que cuando esté listo, llegarán cantidades ingentes de turistas al west rim, supongo que para descongestionar el South Rim, saturadísimo de gente.

Resumiendo, estupenda experiencia con Scenic Airlines, totalmente recomendable. Espero que te haya merecido la pena leerte este ladrillaco ;)

Review Text:
The tour itself is good, the Grand Canyon is definitely a sight to see - the problem is the company running the tour.

We had booked a Grand Canyon tour from Las Vegas. First problem was the pickup from our hotel - 45 minutes late, and after a phone call to see where they were. Then we arrive at Scenic, and are informed of another delay, this time over an hour. They blame the second delay on a traffic jam - of which there was no evidence on our commute to their offices. We suspect they forgot about us and shifted us on a later tour. The result of the above is that we missed the show that we had booked for the evening.

Couple the above with their transportation managers unhelpful attitude and refusal to help us get a faster drop off, a tardy response to my written complaint (which seemed to be a standard response saying delays happen, but they take no responsibility), our overall impression is rather go with another company (and not Papillon as they are the same company)

Review Title: Bad service and rude staff - Poorly organised and amateur
Review Text:
A party of 4 of us took the Grand Voyager tour in June 2008. The cost for 4 people being nearly $1300. You would expect with that sort of price that your tour would be organise properly. The scenery was great but the tour was poorly organised.

We enjoyed or scenic flight although the planes look very old and less than well kept. On arrival at the canyon rim we were delayed by 30 minutes on our helicopter tour to the base of the canyon and ended up standing in the 100 degree heat while we waited for the company to organise our flight to the base of the canyon. When we landed at the base of the canyon you are pointed in the general direction of the river and told to find your own way down to the boat which is about 500ft down a rock track - the whole way along people coming up were asking us the way back to the helicopter pad. No clear path or directions marked on the hazardous trail.

The boat trip was not just that - no commentary to speak of - before returning you to the river bank and you are left to find your own way back up the hill.

This part of tour was OK but it went all wrong when we returned to the canyon rim via helicopter. We were met at the heli pad by a young lady who passed us a ticket and told us to get on the bus and get off at the second stop - the ticket was our lunch ticket. Written on the top of the ticket was 12.30. No explanation was given that this was time we were to return from the canyon rim bus tour to catch our flight back. The ticket was our lunch ticket so we assumed it was our lunch time and had our lunch at 12.30 and returned to the airport by bus at 1.15. At this time we were told that we had missed our flight back and the next one was 4pm. We explained this would mean we would miss our shows that night and we were told in the shorted possible way by the company representative that was 'tough luck' and they would do nothing about. We explained we were not informed of our need to be back at 12.30pm and they could not care less - in fact the insolence and rudeness of the staff would have to be the worst i have ever encountered. It was not until we made quite a scene that the even tried to get us an earlier flight (to no avail) - customer service was sadly lacking. I have travelled all over the world and this is my 3rd time to the Grand Canyon and never have I enountered a poorly organised tour or service this bad - even in 3rd world countries.

We were told that on our return on the 4pm flight that they would have a bus waiting to take us directly to our hotel so we could at least try to get to our show. When we returned on the flight this was not even organised. We were delayed another 30 minutes waiting for our bus. We missed our showtime which meant we lost $520 worth of show tickets.

On complaining to the company they simply refused to do anything about it - I called customer service several times before I managed to get hold of them. When asked why they hadn't call back i was informed that as we were international tourists they were unable to call international cellular numbers. This meant that I wore the cost of the calls made to complain - a total of $67 worth of calls. So a tour that should have taken 6 to 8 hours actually took 11 hours and ended up costing us $587 more that the $1300 dollars it was supposed to. A grand total of $1857 - I could have spent this is with another tour company who would provided us with personalised professional service.

You would have to be insane to trust your money, time and safety to them to professionally conduct a tour. I am one very unhappy customer as are my travelling companions. Unfortunately the company have my money and I have no way of getting it back. Try a different company - not Papillon thats the same organisation.
